description: Non-profit administration, communications, customer service Position: National Gift Processing and Data Entry Coordinator Position Type: Contract, one-year, full-time. Organization: Canadian Parks and Wilderness Society Location: Ottawa, Ontario. Hybrid work environment. Required to be in the office 3 days a week. Reliable high-speed video-enabled internet access is required. A dedicated quiet workspace is required. Language: Bilingual in English and French Preferred – written, oral, and comprehension. Salary Range: $46,000 - $51,000 per annum, based on experience. Benefits: 3 weeks of vacation, plus an office closure between Christmas and New Year, and up to 10 sick days per year. Comprehensive medical and dental benefits, matching RRSP program after probationary period. Posting Date: March 16th , 2026 Closing Deadline for Applications: March 31st, 2026 Start Date: April 15th, 2026 About the Organization Canadian Parks and Wilderness (cpaws.org) is a national charitable organization with 13 chapters across Canada, almost 100 staff, and hundreds of volunteers who have helped to protect over half a million square kilometers of Canada’s public land and water, since 1963. Our conservation vision is to protect at least half of Canada’s public land and water in a framework of reconciliation – for the benefit of both wildlife and humans. CPAWS is based on the unceded and unsurrendered lands of the Anishinabe Algonquin Nation, and works in both unceded and treaty lands of First Nations, Métis and Inuit throughout the country known as Canada. CPAWS is committed to operating in a way that upholds justice, equity, diversity and inclusion (JEDI). We are also working to ensure our office is an inclusive and safe place for people from diverse backgrounds. About the Role Reporting to the National Manager, Data Integrity & Analytics, the National Gift Processing and Data Entry Coordinator’s primary role will be gift processing and database management, playing a key role in ensuring the accuracy and integrity of donor data and the maintenance of CPAWS’s fundraising software system, Raiser’s Edge. Your contributions include processing in-house and online donations, reconciling donations (cash, cheques, and credit cards), maintaining donor records, and responding to donor inquiries. This position works closely with all departments at the CPAWS National Office and our regional chapters to maintain and enhance comprehensive databases which support various departmental and organizational needs. The successful applicant has excellent communication and customer service skills, and knowledge of database management. They have strong attention to detail and exceptional organizational skills, and can adapt quickly while maintaining a clear focus on deadlines and outcomes. Responsibilities Donation Processing – 70% Process and record charitable gifts, including cash, cheques, credit card and direct deposit donations, following proper fund coding. Process Corporate Donations, Bequest, and other unrestricted/restricted donations as needed, following CPAWS Budget Allocation Policy. Process Foundation Grants and Donor-Advised Funds following the corresponding chapter designation and CPAWS Grant unrestricted/restricted structure. Import and process all online donations received via the online platforms: Engaging Networks, Canada Helps, PayPal Giving Fund, Donate a Car, Benevity, and Charitable Impact. Review bank statements weekly and prepare gift processing batches for Electronic Fund Transfer (EFT) deposits. Reconcile offline and online deposits to the bank to ensure they balance; operate various payment gateway portals to obtain reports and donor lists and to process, balance and reconcile donations. Identify, investigate and resolve discrepancies in Donor profiles and Gift records, contacting donors/vendors when needed. File gift batches, control reports, and donation backups (Electronically and In-house) and retain supporting documentation and records for all donations ensuring compliance with CRA rules and regulations. Serve as the Data Team Lead for the CPAWS Monthly Donor Processing Program, including inhouse credit card and direct debit files. Maintain accurate monthly donor records in Raiser’s Edge and across digital engagement platforms. Process monthly donations through multiple channels, including credit card, direct deposit, and online portals. Review and reconcile monthly donor transactions against banking systems to ensure accuracy. Record and process donations received through telephone CPAWS Telemarketing Monthly Donor campaigns. Donor Database Management and Donor Inquiries – 20% Ensure accurate and timely data entry and update biographical data and contact information into the donor database. Provide exceptional customer service, responding to donor inquiries related to monthly payment updates, tax receipts, and general program information received by email or phone. Follow up with monthly donors for payment updates, payment declines and upgrades (Mail, Email, by Phone). Reissue tax receipt and cancel Tax receipt when applicable Liaise with Chapters about any donor requests or Chapter deposits. Maintain return mail and update donor profiles in Raiser's Edge accordingly. Take part in Quality Control efforts by assisting in database clean-ups. Perform regular data clean-up and integrity checks to ensure data accuracy Investigating inconsistencies and resolving discrepancies when gift processing/ data entry errors arise. Generate reports and/or queries from Raiser’s Edge as requested. Assist Database Troubleshooting – continuing support and other knowledge resources. Continuous learning of databases and new systems RENEXT WEBVIEW. Import and update Donor Information via Telemarking, NCOA, SMS and other external lists. General Data Team Administrative Support - 10% Assist in the preparation of the annual audit: printing, scanning, and filing. Ensure that complete and total donor records are always maintained and archived. Work closely with team members to help support the needs of various departments related to gift processing and the database. Train new staff in donation processing and database management, ensuring consistency and compliance with CPAWS standards. Accountability and Authority National Gift Processing and Data Entry Coordinator will work from the CPAWS National office in Ottawa, and report to the National Manager, Data Integrity & Analytics. They will work closely with the Finance Team, Development Team, and CPAWS Chapters, and be the main point of contact with our monthly donors who require assistance. This position requires compliance with the policies and procedures of CPAWS and the Canadian Revenue Agency. All staff are accountable through the staff structure to the National Executive Director for the planning and delivery of programs and services for which they are responsible. The National Executive Director is responsible for staff management and development, and the effectiveness of programs and services within the priorities and budgets approved by the Board. The Human Resources Policy guides the National Executive Director in the day-to-day management of the organization. All CPAWS staff will ensure they have read, understand and adhere to the policy manual. Qualifications & Expectations Essential Assets The successful candidate will be passionate about protecting nature in Canada and will have some knowledge of Canada’s commitment to reconciliation with First Nations, Inuit, and Métis peoples of Canada. Experience working with Blackbaud Raiser’s Edge (or similar donor CRM), including data entry, record maintenance, and donation processing and reconciliation. At least 3 years of data processing and customer service experience, or relevant studies combined with related experience. Strong technical skills in MS 365 (Excel, Word, Teams, SharePoint). Experience handling cash, cheques, and credit card details. An effective communicator both in writing and verbally, with strong interpersonal skills. Exceptionally organized with excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy. Solid time-management and multi-tasking abilities, with the ability to meet deadlines. An inclusive, collegial, and collaborative work ethic with strong teamwork skills. Ability and willingness to adapt to changing priorities and deadlines. Nice to Have Experience working or volunteering in the non-profit/charitable sector. Knowledge of fundraising and solicitation practices. Knowledge of CRA Receipting guidelines. Post-secondary degree or diploma in a related field. Bilingualism is considered a strong asset. Application Submission and Hiring Process CPAWS is committed to a workforce that reflects the diversity of the populations we serve. We encourage applications from all qualified individuals, including applicants from all cultures, racialized communities, abilities, diverse sexual and gender identities, and others who may contribute to equitable representation and diversity of perspectives and ideas. We are committed to a selection process and work environment that is inclusive and barrier-free. Please contact us if you require additional support at any stage of the recruitment process at info@cpaws.org . To apply, please do it through this link, filling out your information and submitting a cover letter and resume saved into a single PDF with the file name LAST NAME_DataCoordinator by March 31st, 2026. Please mention you saw this at GoodWork.ca. We thank all candidates for their interest in the position. Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis, as we are looking to fill this position quickly.
summary: This role is responsible for the accurate processing of charitable gifts and meticulous management of donor data within the Canadian Parks and Wilderness Society, ensuring data integrity for fundraising efforts across national and regional operations.

description: Evergreen is seeking a Director, Fundraising to join our team. We are a national non-profit transforming public spaces in our cities for the health of people and our planet. With over 30 years of championing urban sustainability, we see the potential of our cities to solve some of the biggest issues facing our time and believe that our public spaces are the key to unlocking it. We see beyond the spaces that exist today and imagine them transformed into places where people and nature thrive. The Evergreen Brick Works site, where our head office is located, is built on the sovereign territory and waterways of the Haudenosaunee, Wendat, and Anishinaabe Nations. These nations continue to be the original governments, continuing leaders and decision makers that govern these lands. The territory is governed by Treaty 13 signed by the Mississaugas of the Credit. Treaties remind everyone of our mutual responsibilities to these Nations and the many First Nations, Métis, and Inuit who call this land home. Why Evergreen? In staff engagement surveys, Evergreen employees consistently report that their colleagues are one of the best things about working here. What else is in it for you? A reduced work week (4.5 days) for all full-time staff. Flexible workdays that align with your life needs and role responsibilities. Paid vacation, 3 paid personal days (Evergreen Days), and a paid day off on your birthday. Employer-paid extended health care and dental benefits, including a Health Care Spending Account and access to mental health resources. Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that support staff who are Indigenous, racialized, or 2SLGBTQ+, as well as ERGs for allyship learning, and to support caregivers of all kinds. Active workplace committees, including Health & Safety, IDEA, and Employee Engagement. Access to informal and formal skills development and resume building opportunities. A beautiful head office location surrounded by nature at Evergreen Brick Works, with a free shuttle bus from Broadview Station. Key Accountabilities A day-in-the-life of this role might include: Planning and overseeing a robust multi-year fundraising program with a focus on identifying, cultivating, securing and stewarding principal, major and planned gifts from a diverse community of corporate, foundation, and individual donors, in alignment with Evergreen’s strategy. Leading planning and strategy for the department by setting ambitious fundraising targets and establishing department goals and metrics, in partnership with the Chief Advancement Officer. Working closely with Board members, senior volunteers and external development advisors to support fundraising targets both through formalized committees as well as informal networks. Collaborating with senior leadership in assessing and developing the organization’s strategic and financial goals, and helping to develop approved program budgets. Developing and leading strategic fundraising campaigns, including major capital projects, as necessary. Building and supporting a positive and productive team culture, ensuring all Development department members have a clear, common vision, and that they are well supported in their goals. Establishing expense budgets and maintain expenditure oversight for the Development department. Representing Evergreen at events and meetings to strengthen relationships and create awareness of our programs and position in the marketplace. Analyzing trends in fundraising, identifying opportunities and challenges, and develop strategies to ensure that Evergreen’s plans reflect the direction and demands of the marketplace. Incorporating an anti-oppressive framework into your fundraising. What You’ll Bring Success in this role will be supported by the following target qualifications and core competencies: Diploma/bachelor’s degree in fundraising, public relations, marketing, management, business or a related field, or equivalent work experience. 8 to 10 years prior major gifts and/or capital campaign experience. A track record of achieving targets and closing major, multi-year commitments through relationship building, persistence, and dedicated donor stewardship. Strong Moves Management skills. Demonstrated success in planning and implementing fundraising strategies. Very strong communication and people skills; able to interact and build relationships with a wide variety of individuals including CEOs, philanthropists, and high-level volunteers. Excellent project management and organizational skills, and the ability to manage multiple projects while leading a team. Enjoying the “sales” element of fundraising and possess an ability to bring enthusiasm and inspiration to external pitches and prosect meetings. Proven experience in leading and motivating a development or sales team, with a track record of effectively developing and mentoring others. Possess a strong Toronto-based network, but with an ability to reach beyond the Greater Toronto Area to a national audience. Experience using fundraising software (i.e. Raiser’s Edge, Salesforce) and strong Microsoft Office Suite skills. You might have the following assets: CFRE credentials or actively pursuing. Experience closing gifts in the 6- and 7-figure range. Knowledge of placemaking. Experience working in capital campaign fundraising environments. Aren’t sure if you check every requirement on this list? That’s ok! We are still interested in hearing from you. We’d love to learn more about how your unique experience might make you a great addition to Evergreen. Still Interested? Here are some other things you should know! This is a full-time salaried role to fill a vacant position. The target hire rate for this role is $120,000 to $130,000. To ensure equity and transparency, our target hire rates are real and are not flexible. If this posted rate does not meet your needs, we ask that you save your application for a time when there is a role and salary that is a fit for you. The paid vacation allocation for this role is 20 days. This role is supervised by the CAO and has at least one direct report. This role regularly collaborates with the CEO. Working Conditions: Position is based out of Evergreen’s head office at Evergreen Brick Works in Toronto. Hybrid work environment with on-site presence required for certain events/meetings. It is expected that a significant portion of time will be spent meeting with current and prospective funders, in person or virtually. Regular hours, Monday to Friday (flexible) with occasional evenings and weekends for events, meetings, or in times of heavy deadlines. Our Recruitment Process Interested applicants should submit their candidacy by Sunday, May 3, 2026. Please limit your resume to three pages. Please also include a cover letter to introduce yourself and to give us further context on your job history and skills you’d like to highlight. Candidates selected for an interview will be contacted directly by a member of our People & Culture team. There will be at least one interview for this position, with a high likelihood of a second interview. We are committed to ensuring that all applicants are notified when the role has been filled so that you aren’t left wondering about the position. We’re always learning, so please reach out at any stage of the application process if you require support or adaptations. Evergreen is committed to fostering an inclusive and accessible work environment. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from all qualified individuals. In accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA) and the Ontario Human Rights Code, Evergreen will provide accommodations throughout the recruitment cycle to applicants who request them. Evergreen uses a people-focused approach to evaluating applicants. We do not utilize artificial intelligence during the recruitment process.
summary: The Director, Fundraising plans and oversees a multi-year fundraising program focusing on securing major gifts from diverse donors, developing strategy, leading campaigns, and fostering a productive team culture for a national non-profit.

job_title: Animateur ou animatrice des jardins collectfs
organization: La Maison de Quartier de Villeray
description: OFFRE D’EMPLOI Animateur(trice) de jardin communautaire Organisme Maison de Quartier Villeray (MQV) Lieu : quartier Villeray, Montréal — divers sites de jardins et bacs Statut : poste saisonnier — avril à octobre Horaire : environ 28–35 h/semaine (horaire flexible, quelques événements inclus) Salaire à discuter selon l’expérience (selon l’échelle salariale de l’organisme) Entrée en poste vers 15 avril NOTRE ORGANISME La Maison de Quartier Villeray (MQV) est un organisme communautaire ancré au cœur du quartier Villeray depuis plusieurs décennies. Engagée à favoriser le bien-être, la solidarité et l’inclusion, la MQV offre des services et des espaces de rassemblement qui répondent aux besoins réels des résidents et des familles. Parmi ses projets phares, les jardins collectifs constituent de véritables lieux de vie : ils brisent l’isolement, facilité l’accès à une alimentation saine et locale, et créent des liens durables entre les générations. DESCRIPTION DU POSTE Sous la supervision de la coordination, l’assistant(e) agricole et animateur(trice) de jardin communautaire aura pour mission principale de dynamiser les espaces de jardinage collectif en mettant l’accent sur la participation des personnes aînées du quartier. Ce rôle hybride combine habilement une dimension technique horticole et une dimension humaine d’animation sociale, afin de briser l’isolement tout en facilité l’accès à une alimentation saine et locale. Volet 1 – Animation et mobilisation (social) • Accueillir, accompagner et mobiliser les participant(e)s aîné(e)s dans toutes les étapes des activités de jardinage (semis, entretien, récolte). • Créer un environnement inclusif, sécuritaire et convivial propice aux échanges intergénérationnels et interculturels. • Concevoir et animer des ateliers thématiques adaptés : jardinage de balcon, conservation des récoltes, herbes médicinales, compostage, etc. • Collaborer avec l’équipe pour intégrer les récoltes aux cuisines collectives et aux activités de distribution alimentaire de la MQV. • Sensibiliser les participant(e)s aux bonnes pratiques écologiques et à l’alimentation saine. Volet 2 — Gestion horticole (technique) • Planifier le calendrier de culture saison par saison : rotation des cultures, choix des variétés, semis, transplantation, récolte. • Coordonner l’approvisionnement en semences, terreau, intrants et matériel horticole. • Superviser et assurer l’entretien quotidien des jardins et bacs (arrosage, désherbage, compostage, fertilisation) en mode participatif. • Veiller au bon état des outils, à la propreté et à la sécurité des lieux sur l’ensemble des sites. • Appuyer la production maraichère en serre et jardin, et contribuer à la pérennité des aménagements. Volet 3 – Administration et rayonnement • Documenter la participation, tenir un registre des activités et rédiger un bilan de fin de saison. • Participer aux réunions d’équipe et collaborer activement avec les autres intervenant(e)s de la MQV. • Contribuer à la visibilité du projet (réseaux sociaux, infolettre, affichage dans le voisinage). • Soutenir les partenariats locaux (banques alimentaires pour les surplus, visites pédagogiques avec les écoles, etc.). Volet 4 — Gestion administrative et Financière • Aider l’administration à la recherche de financement : rédiger des demandes de subventions (ex: programme Éco-quartier, fondations privées, Ville de Montréal). • Aider l’administration à la gestion budgétaire : suivre les dépenses, gérer les factures et respecter les enveloppes allouées aux semences, outils et salaires. • Aider l’administration à la reddition de comptes : produire les rapports d’activités pour les bailleurs de fonds et le conseil d’administration. PROFIL RECHERCHÉ Expérience et formation: • Formation ou expérience pertinente en agriculture urbaine, horticulture écologique, agronomie ou domaine connexe. • Expérience en animation de groupe, idéalement auprès d’une clientèle aînée ou de groupes diversifiés. • Intérêt marqué pour le travail communautaire et l’approche participative. Compétences clés: • Solides connaissances pratiques en culture maraichère : semis, compostage, gestion des sols, désherbage écologique. • Capacités relationnelles : écoute active, patience, empathie et pédagogie. • Sens de l’organisation et autonomie dans la gestion des tâches et du calendrier. • Esprit d’initiative et potentialité à travailler en équipe dans un milieu dynamique. Langues • Maîtrise du français (parlé et écrit) — requis. • La connaissance d’une autre langue (anglais, arabe, créole, espagnol, etc.) est un atout dans la diversité de Villeray. Autres atouts • Capacité à travailler en extérieur par tous les temps et à effectuer des tâches physiques (port de charges, etc.). • Connaissance du réseau communautaire de Villeray ou intérêt pour le quartier. • Permis de conduire valide (atout). CONDITIONS DE TRAVAIL Type de poste : poste saisonnier — avril à octobre (7 mois) Horaire : environ 28 à 35 h/semaine, horaire flexible incluant quelques événements Salaire à discuter selon l’expérience — échelle salariale de la MQV Lieu de travail Multiples sites dans le quartier Villeray, Montréal Entrée en poste : à préciser Milieu stimulant, humain, ancré dans la communauté : diversité culturelle et intergenérationnelle COMMENT POSTULER ? Faites parvenir votre curriculum vitae et une lettre de motivation à : Courriel : orgacom@mqvilleray.ca Objet : Candidature Animateur(trice) de jardin Seul(e)s les candidat(e)s retenu(e)s pour une entrevue seront contacté(e)s. Nous remercions toutes les personnes de l’intérêt manifesté pour ce poste. description: Land care, stewardship, ecological restoration Position: Land Stewardship Coordinator — Restoration Organization: Kawartha Land Trust Location: Peterborough, Ontario / Hybrid Reports to: Land Stewardship Manager Compensation: Coordinator band $45,000–$65,000/annually, plus benefits Type: 1.0 FTE Permanent (35 hours/week) Overview Kawartha Land Trust (KLT) is a land conservation charity that protects natural and working lands for future generations. Our mission is to care for the lands entrusted to us and help others protect the land they love in the Kawarthas. Founded in 2001, KLT protects and cares for thousands of acres of ecologically diverse lands. Our public access nature reserves welcome thousands of residents and visitors each year and our community events provide experiential and educational opportunities in nature. All land in the Kawarthas is interconnected. KLT’s growing Partners in Conservation program allows us to increase our impact for nature on our shared landscape by working with landowners on land care initiatives throughout the region. With your support and that of our donors, volunteers, and funders, we can ensure more natural spaces in the Kawarthas are preserved forever. KLT works within Michi Saagiig Nishnaabeg territory. We are committed to strengthening our understanding of our treaty responsibilities and finding opportunities to collaborate with Williams Treaties First Nations in the spirit of reciprocity. The Opportunity Kawartha Land Trust is currently recruiting for a Land Stewardship Coordinator — Restoration to support the delivery of active restoration projects across several KLT-protected properties. The successful candidate will be a self-starter with the ability to work independently while also contributing to a collaborative team environment. The ideal candidate is highly organized and solutions-oriented with a strong ability to prioritize tasks and address challenges effectively. They demonstrate a solid understanding of ecological functions, restoration practices, and approaches to building resilience in rare and/or at-risk ecosystems. This includes experience with hands-on restoration techniques and the ability to dynamically manage ecosystems while providing oversight and coordination for teams of staff and volunteers. Tasks and Responsibilities Coordination of Volunteers You will work closely with KLT’s Volunteer Coordinator to: ● Identify general land care needs and opportunities for volunteers as they relate to restoration and seed based objectives ● Develop and work closely with established teams of volunteers (approx. 25-50 people) to conduct land care work and foster the development of teams to complete enhanced land care objectives ● Track volunteer involvement Planning & Tracking Land Care Program ● In collaboration with the Land Stewardship Manager, prepare annual work plan, including establishing conservation targets ● Project coordination, including development of field schedule, planning workdays, communication with other staff and volunteers ● Tracking annual budget expenditures (~$50,000/year) ● Sourcing quotes and coordinating contractors and service providers ● Purchasing supplies and materials ● Tracking, recording, and reporting on work performed using Salesforce database and Arc GIS suite programs ● Reporting on project deliverables to funders Health & Safety ● Organize training and promote safety among volunteers ● Ensure personal and team safety when in the field Land Care of Conservation Properties ● Monitoring of owned conservation lands and conservation easements ● Addressing and dealing with trespass, vandalism, and other threats to conservation values ● Organize logistics for safe and efficient field work ● Recording and reporting on work performed using Salesforce database and Arc GIS suite programs ● Creation and maintenance of trails using chainsaw, hand tools and brush mower ● Use of a motor boat and canoe for monitoring and care of our island properties ● Light carpentry work maintaining built assets such as signage, fencing, parking areas, etc. Habitat Management ● Caring for owned properties and prioritizing conservation values, species at risk habitat, and climate change resilience ● Identification of unique habitat features of conservation concern (rare communities, uncommon species), including species at risk identification ● Using established Best Management Practices (BMP) and practical experience to manage priority invasive plant species, including the use of herbicides, powered and large equipment ● Tree, shrub, wildflower, and grass planting ● Seed collection, processing, and scattering ● Carrying out site preparation for restoration actions, including forest thinning, brush management, burn break creation, tilling, and mowing ● Surveying restoration areas and conducting inventories to track success including rough ELC typing, vegetative quality assessment, and preferred species density surveys ● Assist with the collection and storage of data including ecological inventory data, GIS and GPS data, photos and the preparation of reports and applications Representing KLT Everyone at Kawartha Land Trust is responsible for being a positive ambassador for our mission and vision. The ability to be a friendly and authentic representative of our organization is very important to success in the role with specific roles and responsibilities such as: ● Under the direction of the Land Stewardship Manager, coordinate enhanced access with users on conservation lands ● General KLT ambassador for the general public and volunteers Other duties as required. Desired Level of Skills and Experience Ability to prioritize and simultaneously coordinate a number of projects across multiple field locations Highly organized and able to stay flexible with a changing environment At least three seasons of field work in land care or restoration Experience coordinating and overseeing teams of volunteers or staff in the field Experience using herbicides, participating in prescribed burns, and managing grassland plant communities is considered an asset Work experience showing a comfort with outdoor work, a positive attitude in adverse weather conditions, and comfort navigating off-trail. The position will require ability to walk long distances and carry equipment Experience with rough carpentry, landscaping, tree felling and pruning, tree planting, fence building, installing signage, and vegetation management Experience towing a trailer and securing equipment on field vehicles (canoes, trailer contents) as well as other small vehicles (ATV, UTV, etc.) Practical experience, and good proficiency, with administrative tasks to support field work such as data collection and note taking, data entry and file management. Experience with databases is an asset Understanding of risk management and its applications in the field Team player with the ability to work effectively with staff and volunteers Ability to learn new skills quickly, problem solve and know when to ask for support Desired Level of Education A degree or diploma in natural resource management, forestry, ecological restoration, environmental science or studies, biology, or related disciplines is an asset (demonstrated relevant experience or ways of knowing will also be considered) Additional Criteria Ability to lift/carry 45lbs and work for extended periods of time outdoors Must have a valid G2 license and access to a personal vehicle (mileage will be compensated) In possession of, or ability to obtain, a boater’s licence Legally entitled to work in Canada Chainsaw license and experience Must be prepared to work some evening and weekends Must be prepared to work alone in the field on occasion Must have a personal cellphone with ability to use a data plan (will provide monthly phone allowance) Benefits Ability to flex time throughout the week and work in a hybrid work environment (in-office and remote) 10 paid wellness days annually Competitive health and dental benefits package after probationary period GRSP with 3% employer match after probationary period Working in a supportive office with passionate people who care about the environment and their co-workers Opportunities and Perks of the Position Contributing to lasting conservation projects in the Kawarthas! Spending time outdoors in protected nature areas with access to beautiful views, high biodiversity areas Being part of a network of dedicated environmental professionals. Opportunities to participate in surveys and fieldwork to protect/enhance habitat for wildlife, including species at risk, and overall ecosystem health; opportunities to learn and practice application of a variety of field work protocols Access to training opportunities with professionals in a wide range of areas Application Process Your application should include a resume and a covering letter as one document which specifically addresses how your skills and qualifications relate to the job tasks and responsibilities. The cover letter should be no more than one page long. Send application as a PDF or Word document with the following file name format: Last Name, First Name_ Land Stewardship Coordinator. Email your cover letter and resume in one document to Kawartha Land Trust at info@kawarthalandtrust.org by 12 p.m. (noon), April 6th, 2026, with the subject line “Land Stewardship Coordinator-Restoration". Please mention you saw this at GoodWork.ca. Anticipated start date for the successful applicant would be May 4, 2026.
summary: This role coordinates and supports ecological restoration projects across protected properties, engaging volunteers and managing project logistics for a land conservation charity.

job_title: Coordination – Offre à la communauté (2e appel)
description: Le 7 A NOUS est un OBNL porteur du projet connu sous le nom de Bâtiment 7, un lieu collectif acquis de chaude lutte par la population de Pointe-Saint-Charles pour en faire pôle de projets et de services à la communauté. Il est aussi le gardien de sa mission et le responsable de la mise en oeuvre de ses objectifs de transformation sociale, économique, politique et culturelle. Le 7 À NOUS s’est doté d’un fonctionnement par cercles, non hiérarchique, visant l’implication directe de ses membres et l’autonomie. Ouvert depuis sept ans, le climat qui y règne en est un de développement, de transformation constante et d’adaptation. Les personnes embauchées doivent être fortement motivées à travailler dans un tel cadre. Le Bâtiment 7 est un immeuble de près de 90 000 pieds carrés dont environ 23 000 sont occupés et rénovés. Il est occupé par plusieurs projets en plus des ateliers du B7 : bois, mécanique, céramique, vélo, studio photo et impression numérique. L’offre à la communauté fait référence aux services et activités offerts au Bâtiment 7, notamment les espaces de location, les sept ateliers du B7, les activités phares (party de financement, Marché de Léon, Portes ouvertes et Fête du B7), la programmation large de l’ensemble des occupants et l’accueil du B7. L’offre à la communauté est ce qui rend vivant le Bâtiment 7, permet de générer des revenus autonomes, tout en ayant des activités accessibles et gratuites pour la communauté. Responsabilités En collaboration avec le Cercle offre à la communauté et le Cercle des ateliers, nous sommes à la recherche d’une personne compétente en coordination, qui vibre pour les activités du B7 et souhaite en porter le déploiement et la cohérence. Les responsabilités du poste sont de : 1. Coordonner le Cercle offre et le Cercle des ateliers par l’élaboration et le suivi du plan d’action du Cercle et par le suivi de ses différents comités. 2. Participer au Conseil de coordination. 3. Soutenir l’équipe salariée relevant de l’Offre par le soutien à l’élaboration et au suivi des plans de travail; par l’organisation de rencontres d’équipe; par la participation aux processus d’embauche et d’évaluation. 4. Faire avancer le déploiement de l’Offre du Bâtiment 7 par : a. la détermination de cibles et le suivi des résultats budgétaires; b. les réflexions d’ensemble sur les activités présentes et leur arrimage; c. l’actualisation constante du modèle; d. la participation à l’élaboration d’un plan de communication. 5. Coordonner la programmation au Bâtiment 7 en recueillant les informations relatives à l’offre et aux autres projets, en réalisant un calendrier coordonné et en mettant sur pied des instances ad hoc fonctionnelles pour la réalisation des activités phares. 6. Coordonner l’accueil du Bâtiment 7 : en s’assurant de la mobilisation des membres, de la présence de bénévoles et que l’accueil dispose de tous les outils nécessaires. 7. Réaliser diverses tâches connexes en fonction des besoins de l’organisation. 8. Participer aux réunions d’équipe et à la vie démocratique du 7 À NOUS. Compétences recherchées – Compétence en coordination de projets complexes et d’équipe; – Capacité de conception, de planification et de déploiement stratégique des opérations; – Expérience significative de gestion dans le milieu artistique, culturel ou communautaire; – Expérience dans un milieu autogéré; – Capacité de rédaction et de communication verbales et écrites; – Connaissance du fonctionnement démocratique du Bâtiment 7, un atout; – Français écrit et parlé, capacité de communiquer en anglais. Intérêts – Intérêt pour la mission et le développement du Bâtiment 7; – Travailler dans un contexte d’autogestion ou en collectif; – Travailler en accord avec des orientations collectives, en collaboration avec les autres membres de l’organisme. Conditions ★ Salaire : 27,40 $/h ★ Horaire : 35 h/semaine, horaire flexible qui requiert parfois une certaine présence le soir et la fin de semaine pendant l’ouverture du bâtiment. ★ 4 semaines de vacances + 2 semaines de vacances durant le temps des fêtes. ★ 10 journées de congé personnel + 9 journées fériées. ★ Régime de retraite. ★ Durée du contrat : 1 an avec possibilité de permanence par la suite (évaluation de probation au terme de 6 mois). ★ Lieu de travail : Bâtiment 7, Pointe-Saint-Charles. Critères de priorisation Par le biais de sa mission, de son emplacement et de ses pratiques, le Bâtiment 7 revendique la pleine inclusion sociale et économique des personnes vivant une marginalisation imposée. Nous désirons promouvoir leur participation et leur leadership au sein de notre communauté. Nous encourageons donc les résident.es de Pointe Saint-Charles, notamment les résident.es de longue date, et les membres de diverses communautés culturelles et sous-représentées à postuler. Domaine: Administration et gestion, Arts, culture et divertissement, Service clientèle et soutien administratif 35 heures / semaine Jour, Temps plein Emploi Permanent En présentiel

description: Toronto environmental organizations, Leadership Hiring: Executive Director Organization: Toronto Environmental Alliance Location: Toronto, Ontario / Hybrid Toronto’s leading environmental organization seeks an Executive Director. Attention non-profit leaders and changemakers: The Toronto Environmental Alliance, a nationally recognized leader at the intersection of local environmental advocacy, social inclusion and well being is recruiting for a new permanent, full-time Executive Director to lead the organization into its next phase. About TEA: For over 37 years, TEA has campaigned locally to find solutions to Toronto's urban environmental problems. TEA is a not-for-profit that is recognized Canada-wide for advancing successful municipal policies on climate change, waste reduction, and intersecting issues that are critical to health and well-being of Toronto residents. We work with communities across Toronto to build a greener, healthier, and more equitable city. TEA is a non-partisan organization. The Opportunity: TEA is entering an exciting phase of finalizing a strategic plan to guide our work forward. We are seeking a leader who will seize this unique opportunity to work with TEA’s board and staff to shape and implement the future directions of TEA’s work. TEA is looking for an Executive Director who is passionate about environmental justice and engaging the public in local environmental policy. We wish to hire a leader with significant experience working in the not-for-profit sector or comparable community sectors, who understands how change happens politically and socially. The Executive Director is a hands-on leader, who manages a staff team, oversees the internal operations of the organization, ensures strategic alignment across projects, and works with the team to develop and execute sustainable and mission-aligned fundraising strategies. The Executive Director cultivates and maintains TEA’s excellent reputation at Toronto City Hall, and builds relationships with supporters, partners, donors and funders. Applying a strong equity analysis and intersectional approach, along with prudent non-profit leadership, the Executive Director is responsible for the following areas of work: Strategy, leadership and organizational development Lead the development and execution of TEA’s external-facing work, impactful environmental and social justice campaigns and communications, in collaboration with the staff team. Work with the Board to finalize TEA’s new Strategic Plan which will set the direction of the organization for success in a rapidly changing economic and political environment. Develop donor and grant based fundraising strategies that will build and maintain relationships that contribute to organizational sustainability. Maintain and expand TEA’s leadership within the broader network of agencies and groups in the environmental advocacy ecosystem. Fundraising and financial planning Ensure TEA has effective strategies in place to achieve its annual fundraising targets and grow diverse revenue streams, including individual giving and institutional and philanthropic grants. Lead TEA’s annual planning and budgeting process, and support the staff team to develop and monitor quarterly work-plans. Manage organizational finances, oversee TEA’s annual audit, and ensure compliance with government not-for-profit requirements. People-management, operations and governance Lead TEA’s staff team of 8 campaigns, communications, and finance personnel, and provide direction, coaching, and performance evaluation to direct reports. Oversee the day-to-day operations of the organization in line with TEA’s goals, strategies, policies and procedures, and develop and maintain workflows, project management and decision-making processes. Support the work of the Board of Directors, by providing regular, open communication, and working collaboratively to develop and implement organizational policies and procedures. Support a healthy and dynamic working environment for all team members. Partnerships and External Relations Oversee TEA’s communications strategy across all areas of work, the development and stewardship of strategic partnerships and relationships with ally organizations, community groups, funders and decision-makers. Represent the organization externally as a primary media spokesperson at City Hall, external forums and meetings, and making public presentations. Proactively seek opportunities for TEA to support and stand in solidarity, with Indigenous nations, organizations and community members, trade unions, and equity-owed residents in advocating for environmental justice. About you The ideal candidate will demonstrate a combination of the following competencies and qualifications: Competencies: Ability to deliver on goals and provide leadership in a complex, multi-stakeholder non-profit environment. The necessary knowledge to deliver on the job responsibilities, and the judgement to seek new knowledge when they need it. Strong analytical skills and experience bridging strategic goals with operational and tactical execution. A collaborative, respectful, and adaptable leadership style. Works comfortably with technology and has experience with cloud-solutions, electronic workflows and virtual collaboration as part of a “hybrid” organization with staff sometimes working remotely and off-site. Compelling communication, with excellent, audience-appropriate oral and written skills. Strategic thinking; excellent judgment and political acuity. Excellent record keeping, financial management, organizational and time management skills including the ability to set priorities and balance competing deadlines and pressures. Demonstrated commitment to environmental justice, social justice and equity. Qualifications: Significant experience (at least five years) in a management role in the not-for-profit or trade-union environment. Direct, relevant experience with advocacy, municipal government relations, and strong knowledge of government policy-making processes. Directly relevant skill and experience in human resources, non-profit finance, governance and compliance. Excellent track record of building collaborative and reciprocal partnerships with community organizations and grassroots groups across sectors. Demonstrated track record of fundraising to achieve annual targets and donor/funder stewardship through philanthropic and public-sector grants and individual giving programs. Post-secondary degree in at least one of the following disciplines: environmental studies, environmental sciences, political science, not-for-profit management, communications, equity studies, or a related discipline (or equivalent lived and professional experience). Terms and Conditions of Employment TEA offers competitive, non-profit compensation. This is a full-time position with a starting salary of $104,000 per annum plus benefits. TEA provides health benefits and generous vacation and paid holiday provisions including a December office closure between Dec 25th and Jan 1st. The Executive Director will have flexibility to work both in office and remotely. In-office attendance (depending on operational needs) at TEA’s office near Queen and Spadina is a requirement of the position. The Executive Director will also be required to attend on-site meetings at Toronto City Hall as well as with funders and stakeholders across the Greater Toronto Area on a regular basis. Given the local focus of the organization and the on-site requirements for the role, the Executive Director is required to reside within the Greater Toronto Area (GTA). The position requires regular evening and occasional weekend work. TEA is filling an upcoming vacancy How to apply Review of applications will continue until the position is filled. To apply, please upload a cover letter and resume by completing the application form at this link. https://forms.gle/BZGrEBkVnxSJKyU79. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis and early applications are encouraged. Please mention you saw this at GoodWork.ca. TEA is committed to providing accommodation for applicants at any stage of the application and hiring process upon request by contacting chair@torontoenvironment.org . TEA is committed to employment equity. We encourage Indigenous people, Black people / people of African descent, racialized people, people with disabilities, people who identify as 2SLGBTQI+, non-binary people and women, to apply. Applicants are encouraged to self-identify their equity-owed identities in their application and/or via email to support us in recognizing the inclusion of diverse identities in our hiring process. We thank all applicants for their interest but only those selected for an interview will be contacted. TEA does not use Artificial Intelligence tools in its recruitment process.
summary: The Executive Director leads a nationally recognized non-profit environmental advocacy organization, driving strategic planning, fundraising, staff management, and external relations to advance local environmental policy and social justice in Toronto.

job_title: Intervenant.e de soutien aux demandeurs d’asile / Refugee Claimant Support Worker
description: Intervenant.e de soutien aux demandeurs d’asile Action Réfugiés Montréal (ARM) est un organisme non gouvernemental à but non lucratif, d’inspiration confessionnelle, qui œuvre depuis plus de 30 ans à la promotion de la justice et à la défense des droits des personnes réfugiées et demandeuses d’asile. Sa mission est d’accompagner les personnes ayant fait une demande d’asile ou obtenu le statut de réfugié, en leur offrant un soutien humain et des services adaptés à leurs besoins, tout en contribuant à sensibiliser la société québécoise et canadienne aux enjeux migratoires actuels. Nos programmes comprennent notamment le soutien aux personnes détenues pour des motifs liés à l’immigration, la réunification familiale, ainsi que des initiatives de sensibilisation du public à travers le jumelage et l’éducation aux droits. Le présent recrutement s’inscrit dans une volonté de renforcer nos interventions dans ce secteur afin d’accroître notre impact dans un contexte migratoire en constante évolution. DESCRIPTION Sous la supervision de la Coordonnatrice du programme Soutien à la détention, l’Intervenant.e de soutien auprès des personnes demandeuses d’asile est responsable d’offrir un accompagnement social et administratif aux personnes concernées ainsi qu’aux personnes migrantes à statut précaire, incluant celles qui ont vécu ou qui sont à risque de vivre une situation de détention pour des raisons migratoires. Principales responsabilités: Fournir un accompagnement approprié aux personnes réfugiées et demandeuses d’asile; Effectuer des prises d’information initiales (par téléphone, courriel ou en personne) en vue de l’évaluation des besoins des personnes bénéficiaires; Répondre aux appels téléphoniques des personnes qui sont détenues et effectuer le suivi de cas individuels; Référer des personnes aux ressources appropriées (juridiques, psychosociaux, médicaux); Veiller à la gestion rigoureuse et confidentielle des données et des comptes rendus d’intervention, en coordination avec l’équipe; Développer et actualiser des outils d’information et de référencement, tout en maintenant un réseau actif avec les ressources communautaires partenaires; Participer à l’identification des priorités de défense des droits ou de sensibilisation; Aider à la préparation et aux suivis des dossiers administratifs des bénéficiaires (permis de travail, papier brun, RAMQ…); Se tenir informé des modifications apportées à la législation et aux politiques en matière d’immigration et de détention; Effectuer des suivis réguliers avec les personnes anciennement détenues, ainsi qu’avec les membres de leur famille, le cas échéant; Responsabilités générales Aider à comptabiliser les données statistiques pertinentes liées aux programmes; Participer au processus de la création des rapports mensuels, trimestriels et annuels; Répondre aux demandes de renseignements générales par téléphone et en personne et faire des références appropriées; Effectuer d’autres tâches assignées par la coordonnatrice et/ou la direction générale. EXIGENCES : Avoir au moins un baccalauréat en travail social, en droit ou dans un domaine connexe; Minimum de 2 années d’expérience dans un poste similaire, idéalement en milieu communautaire ou en contexte de migration; Sensibilité marquée aux réalités vécues par les personnes réfugiées et migrantes, avec une approche empreinte de compassion, d’empathie et de non-jugement; Excellentes aptitudes en communication interpersonnelle et interculturelle; Atout : connaissance du système carcéral canadien; Atout : expérience ou formation en intervention en contexte de détention; Excellente maîtrise du français et de l’anglais. L’espagnol ou l’arabe serait un atout; Bonne maîtrise des outils informatiques (Microsoft Office, Google Workspace). CONDITIONS DE TRAVAIL Poste à temps plein (37,5 h/sem), basé à Montréal. Horaire de jour, avec occasionnellement des activités en fin de semaine. La présence régulière au bureau est requise avec possibilité de télétravail partiel (1 jour/sem). Le salaire offert pour ce poste se situe entre 43,816.50 $ et 48,685.00 $ par année, selon l’expérience et les qualifications. AVANTAGES Le poste offre un régime de soins de santé, un REER avec contribution de l’employeur après 3 mois d’ancienneté, ainsi que 3 semaines de vacances annuelles, et 10 jours de congés personnels. COMMENT POSTULER? Veuillez envoyer une lettre de motivation et un CV à jour par courriel à emplois@actionr.org au plus tard le 20 mars 2026. Ces documents peuvent être soumis en français ou en anglais. Les candidatures sans lettre de motivation ne seront pas considérées. ARM valorise la diversité et l’égalité des chances en emploi. Les personnes issues de parcours migratoires, autochtones, racisées ou appartenant à des groupes marginalisés sont encouragées à postuler. Toutes les candidatures seront examinées équitablement et des accommodements peuvent être offerts sur demande. Refugee Claimant Support Worker Action Réfugiés Montréal (ARM) is a non-profit, faith-inspired organization that has been promoting justice and defending the rights of refugees and asylum seekers for over 30 years. Our mission is to support individuals who have applied for asylum or obtained refugee status by providing personalized assistance and services tailored to their needs, while also raising awareness within Quebec and Canadian society on current migration issues. Our programs include support for individuals detained for immigration-related reasons, family reunification, as well as public awareness initiatives through mentorship and rights education. This recruitment aims to strengthen our interventions in this sector to enhance our impact in an ever-evolving migration context. Position Overview Under the supervision of the Detention Support Program Coordinator, the Asylum Seeker Support Worker is responsible for providing social and administrative support to asylum seekers and other migrants with precarious status, including those who have experienced or are at risk of experiencing detention for migration-related reasons. Key Responsibilities: Provide appropriate support to refugees and asylum seekers; Conduct initial intake (via phone, email, or in person) to assess the needs of beneficiaries; Respond to phone calls from detained individuals and follow up on individual cases; Refer individuals to appropriate resources (legal, psychosocial, medical); Ensure rigorous and confidential management of data and intervention reports in coordination with the team; Develop and update informational and referral tools while maintaining an active network with community partners; Participate in identifying advocacy or awareness priorities; Assist with preparation and follow-up of beneficiaries’ administrative files (work permits, “papier brun,” RAMQ, etc.); Stay informed of changes to immigration and detention laws and policies; Conduct regular follow-ups with formerly detained individuals and, when relevant, with their family members. General Responsibilities: Assist in compiling relevant statistical data related to programs; Contribute to the creation of monthly, quarterly, and annual reports; Respond to general inquiries by phone or in person and provide appropriate referrals; Perform other tasks assigned by the Coordinator and/or Executive Director. Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in social work, law, or a related field; Minimum of 2 years’ experience in a similar role, ideally in a community or migration context; Strong sensitivity to the realities of refugees and migrants, demonstrating compassion, empathy, and a non-judgmental approach; Excellent interpersonal and intercultural communication skills; Asset: knowledge of the Canadian correctional system; Asset: experience or training in detention-related interventions; Fluency in French and English. Spanish or Arabic is an asset; Proficiency in computer applications (Microsoft Office, Google Workspace). Working Conditions: Full-time position (37.5 hours/week), based in Montreal. Daytime schedule with occasional weekend activities. Regular office presence is required, with the possibility of partial remote work (1 day/week). The salary for this position ranges from $43,816.50 to $48,685.00 per year, depending on experience and qualifications, in accordance with the organization’s salary scale. Benefits: The position offers a health care plan, employer-matched RRSP after 3 months of employment, 3 weeks of annual vacation, and 10 personal days. How to Apply: Please submit a cover letter and updated CV by email to emplois@actionr.org no later than March 20, 2026. Documents can be submitted in French or English. Applications without a cover letter will not be considered. Domaine: Santé et services sociaux 37.5 heures / semaine Jour, Temps plein Emploi Contractuel En présentiel, Hybride
summary: L'Intervenant.e de soutien aux demandeurs d’asile chez Action Réfugiés Montréal accompagne socialement et administrativement les personnes réfugiées et migrantes, particulièrement celles ayant vécu ou risquant une détention liée à l'immigration, afin de défendre leurs droits et de sensibiliser le public.

description: Grow food, Organic veggie farming We are seeking interns for our 2026 growing season! Position: Organic Vegetable Farm Intern Farm: Grey Wolf Gardens Location: Cochrane, Northern Ontario Housing: on-farm accommodation (see below) Are you are interested in learning how to grow your own food? Would you like to work with Northern Native communities? Are you interested in improving food security for people in the North? Grey Wolf Gardens is an organic mixed vegetable farm in Northern Ontario that provides fresh organic produce to communities in the North, including 25 Native families through our partnership with the Ininew Friendship Centre. We have an excellent team of young, friendly farm workers, a great farm culture, very comfortable on-farm accomodations, and tons of wild spaces to explore! Learn to grow your own food, make herbal medicines, work with First Nation communities and so much more! Get a taste for Northern living and experience all the beauty that the North has to offer. Working with us, you will learn: Mixing plant starter soil mixes, seed starting, nursery management and seedling care Bed prep for planting Transplanting, direct seeding, and paperpot planting Fertilization, irrigation and weed and pest management Proper harvest technique and post-harvest handling The harvesting of wild medicinal plants and the preparation of herbal products How to drive a tractor and use other machines like a mini-excavator and a BCS walk behind tractor We run a 25 family CSA and run two farmer’s markets. We also have a partnership with the native community, where we manage a demonstration garden on their Cultural Grounds and provide some workshops throughout the season to the community members. The Cultural Grounds is also where traditional ceremonies and activities take place, like sweat lodges, meat smoking, hide preparation and tanning and more. Payment is a $400 weekly stipend. We also offer on-farm accommodation. Our farm staff have their own fully furnished house with all the amenities, as well as use of the farm truck for travel into town. Additionally, we offer unlimited produce from the farm as well as a food stipend for foods purchased from town on top of the labour stipend. We have monthly group dinners and bonfires, and there are lots of things to do in town as well! After a long day on the farm, you’re only a 15 minute drive into town where you can relax on the beach, go for a swim in Lake Commando or grab an ice cream! If you are interested in learning how to grow your own food, making your own herbal medicines, working with Native communities, and being part of an awesome team, get in touch today! If you have any questions or want to discuss the position, don't hesitate to call Luke Dinan at 705 262 9772. Please email your resume + an introduction letter to: greywolfgardens@gmail.com Please mention you saw this at GoodWork.ca.
summary: This internship provides hands-on experience in organic vegetable farming, including planting, harvesting, and equipment operation, while contributing to food security for Northern Native communities and learning about herbal medicines.

job_title: Coordonnateur·trice à l’administration, aux finances et à l’archivage
description: Regroupement Naissances Respectées (RNR) — Montréal (Maison Parent-Roback) Entrée en poste : dès que possible Contrat : jusqu’au 31 août 2027 Le RNR, c’est quoi? Le Regroupement Naissances Respectées (RNR)est un regroupement féministe d’action communautaire autonome principalement composé d’organismes qui offrent des services aux familles dans leur parcours périnatal.La mission du RNR est de promouvoir et de défendre les droits de toute personne vivant la période périnatale, et ce, dans une perspective de justice sociale. Vous cherchez un nouveau défi dans un milieu féministe et collaboratif? Vous aimez quand les choses sont bien structurées, et vous avez un faible assumé pour les tableaux, les suivis et les systèmes qui “tiennent la route”? Vous avez envie de joindre une équipe qui travaille dans un milieu stimulant où sont regroupés sous un même toit des organismes féministes (Maison Parent-Roback)? Venez travailler avec nous! Le mandat Sous la supervision de la direction générale et en étroite collaboration avec le reste de l’équipe de travail, la personne titulaire du poste à la coordination à l’administration, aux finances et à l’archivage a pour mission d’assurer une gestion administrative et financière rigoureuse du RNR, tout en coordonnant un volet d’archivage rendu possible grâce à une subvention dédiée. Elle planifie, organise, supervise et met en place les activités sous sa responsabilité, et contribue au développement et à la solidité de l’organisation grâce à des processus clairs, cohérents et accessibles. TÂCHES ET RESPONSABILITÉS Administration et finances Assurer la tenue de livres : comptes payables/recevables, dépôts, facturation, conciliations bancaires, classement des pièces comptables. Assurer les suivis financiers réguliers : budgets, suivi des dépenses, prévisions, tableaux de bord et rapports internes. Préparer et produire, au besoin, les documents liés à la paie et aux obligations administratives (ex. rapports de taxes, documents de fin d’année, etc.). Collaborer avec la direction générale et/ou la firme comptable aux états financiers annuels, à la vérification et aux redditions de comptes. Soutenir l’équipe dans l’application des procédures administratives (contrats, ententes, documents internes, suivis logistiques). Appuyer la vie démocratique et associative du RNR sur le plan administratif : préparation de documents pour le CA et les comités, suivi de résolutions, archivage des procès-verbaux et documents officiels. Archivage (volet financé par subvention) Coordonner la mise à jour des systèmes de classement et d’archivage (papier et numérique) : structure, nomenclature, accès, sauvegardes, logique documentaire. Organiser le tri, le classement et la numérisation de documents (administratifs, projets, documentation organisationnelle, mémoire du regroupement). Mettre en place ou bonifier une base de données / système de repérage pour assurer une mémoire organisationnelle durable et facile d’accès. Contribuer à l’amélioration de politiques et procédures internes liées à la gestion documentaire et administrative. Collaborer, au besoin, avec un partenaire spécialisé en archivage. Soutien transversal à la direction et à l’équipe Participer aux réunions d’équipe, à la planification et à la reddition de comptes. Assurer un soutien ponctuel à la logistique des activités du RNR (inscriptions, réservations, commandes, soutien technique, etc.). Contribuer au maintien d’un milieu de travail féministe, intersectionnel, bienveillant et cohérent avec les valeurs du RNR. Exigences, connaissances, expériences Formation en administration, comptabilité, gestion, bureautique ou expérience pertinente équivalente (nous reconnaissons aussi les parcours atypiques et l’expérience communautaire). Expérience en administration et/ou finances (milieu communautaire : atout). Aisance avec les outils informatiques (Suite Office / Google) et idéalement un logiciel comptable (ex. Sage 50 : atout). Très bonne connaissance du français écrit et parlé. Connaissance de l’anglais parlé et écrit (un atout). Intérêt ou expérience en archivage, classement, gestion documentaire et structuration de systèmes (atout important). Connaissance de l’écriture épicène ou inclusive (atout). Le profil que nous recherchons Sens de l’organisation et grande rigueur. Autonomie, initiative, capacité à gérer plusieurs dossiers en parallèle. Capacité à structurer, simplifier et rendre les outils accessibles à l’équipe. Esprit d’équipe, habiletés relationnelles, discrétion et fiabilité. Adhésion aux valeurs du milieu communautaire féministe et de l’action communautaire autonome. En rejoignant notre équipe, nous vous offrons : Un taux horaire de départ entre 24,31 $ et 30,38 $, pouvant évoluer jusqu’à 36,15 $ selon les années à l’emploi et les capacités de l’organisme. Une semaine de 28 h Contrat jusqu’au 31 août 2027. Une conciliation famille-travail et le respect du temps de déconnexion dans les communications entre l’équipe. 4 semaines de vacances dès la première année, plus 2 semaines de congé pendant la période des Fêtes (25 décembre au 1er janvier). Accès à un régime de retraite avec 8 % de cotisation de l’employeur et 2 % de l’employé·e (après 3 mois à l’emploi). Un fonds annuel de santé et de bien-être. Des congés pour la famille, les maladies et affaires personnelles. De la formation continue. La proposition vous intéresse? Faites-nous parvenir votre CV et une lettre d’intérêt dès que possible par courriel à rh@naissancesrespectees.org Les entrevues auront lieu en visioconférence dans la semaine du 23 mars pour une entrée en poste dès que possible. Seules les personnes retenues pour une entrevue seront contactées. Nous remercions de leur intérêt toustes les personnes ayant soumis leur candidature Équité en matière d’emploi Les personnes issues de communautés historiquement discriminées et qui font face à des barrières systémiques à l’emploi sont encouragées à appliquer. Cela inclut, mais ne se limite pas, aux communautés suivantes : les femmes, les personnes autochtones, les personnes non binaires, les personnes ayant diverses capacités, les personnes racisées, LGBTQIA2S+ et les personnes socio-économiquement marginalisées.L’équipe est engagée à développer un processus qui favorise l’embauche de personnes appartenant à un ou plusieurs groupes discriminés. Si vous le souhaitez, vous pouvez nous l’indiquer dans votre lettre de motivation. Domaine: Administration et gestion 28 heures / semaine Jour Emploi Temporaire Hybride AVANTAGES SOCIAUX Horaire flexible Café Congés de maladie Congés mobiles Régime de retraite Conciliation travail-vie personnelles
summary: Ce poste assure la gestion administrative, financière et l'archivage rigoureux pour un regroupement féministe d'action communautaire, contribuant à sa solidité organisationnelle et à la promotion des droits périnatals dans une perspective de justice sociale.

location: Toronto/GTA ON. Virtual and In-person. Candidates should live in the GTA.
description: Non-profit Board Position Role: Board Chair Type: non-profit board / unpaid Organization: Let's Hike T.O. Location: Toronto/GTA ON. Virtual and In-person. Candidates should live in the GTA. Let’s Hike T.O. is a registered non-profit organization with the mission to diversify hiking communities through easy access to safe and enjoyable hikes for anyone, with a special focus on actively engaging people of colour, newcomers and young adults. We strongly believe in equity, diversity, and inclusion and try to ensure that our hikes reflect that in every way. Founded in July 2021, since then we have led over 300+ hikes and had 4,000+ people come hiking with us. Our extended volunteer community has 40+ active members. We are a 100% volunteer-run organization so the board plays both a strategic and operational role. This role is a Board position and will work with our team of volunteer board members to guide all aspects of the organization. The Board Chair is an approachable and organized coordinator who oversees volunteers with a balance of guidance and respect. They communicate clearly and effectively, making sure expectations are understood while also listening to feedback. Rather than pushing too hard, they motivate through encouragement and appreciation, ensuring volunteers feel valued and supported. They are mindful of people’s workloads and personal commitments, creating an environment where volunteers can contribute meaningfully without feeling overwhelmed. This role is perfect for someone who: Is passionate about diversity and the outdoors Is a natural at running meetings and ensuring equal participation Enjoys collaborating and building consensus Is highly organized, a strategic thinker, and able to deeply identify with our mission Understands how boards work, grasps the role of the Board Chair well, and has been on a board before Effective communicator Key Responsibilities: Lead board meetings effectively and impartially Set the agenda in collaboration with the Board Support strategic planning and monitor progress toward organizational goals Ensure all board members are actively engaged and informed Facilitate healthy discussions and manage differing opinions Support the board and volunteers in their roles Handle recruitment and training of board members (once a year) Problem solve organizational challenges as they arise Co-plan volunteer appreciation events Provide opportunities for volunteers to feel cared for and appreciated Act as a positive representative of Let’s Hike T.O. and role model at all times Act as a public face of the board when appropriate Time Commitment This role requires 8-10 hours a month plus one monthly virtual board meeting held one day per month from 7 - 8:30pm (TBD). The commitment is for remainder of 2026, with potential for 2027 year comitment. Expectations of all board members: Assist in strategic oversight of the organization and its financial condition Attend, prepare for, and actively participate in the monthly board meetings, with a maximum of two absences allowed per year, provided advance notice is given Attend volunteer recognition events plus at least two hikes Act as a positive representative of Let’s Hike T.O. and a role model at all times Training Required For New Board Members: In-person half day of board training Reading the Let’s Hike T.O. Hike Leader’s Guide to understand how we lead our events Two-hour role specific training with an existing board member EDI training (self paced, online) Benefits Free access to all hikes (first come first serve basis) Free Let’s Hike T.O. merch and discounts (when available) Be a part of an awesome and passionate group of community builders Hike Leader Training (if so desired) How to Apply / Contact To apply, complete this form explaining how you meet the qualities and skills required and we will follow up to have an informal interview with you! Please mention you saw this at GoodWork.ca. We particularly welcome applications from Black and Indigenous People of Colour, newcomers, LGBTQ2S+ people, and all other equity-deserving groups. Thank you for your interest!
summary: This volunteer Board Chair position for Let's Hike T.O., a non-profit, focuses on diversifying hiking communities and requires strategic and operational guidance, volunteer management, and fostering an inclusive environment.

description: Macadam Sud est à la recherche d’un·e travailleur·euse de rue pour l’unité mobile le TROC MACADAM SUD, C’EST QUOI ? Un organisme communautaire offrant 6 volets d’intervention pour accompagner et soutenir les 12-35 ans ainsi toute personne en détresse; Un pilier de sa communauté qui fait ses preuves sur le territoire du Grand Longueuil depuis près de 40 ans ! Approches humaniste, de réduction des méfaits et d’empowerment. Le TROC est un autobus aménagé avec un espace ouvert pour des activités de groupes et un salon fermé pour des rencontres privées. Tu peux venir prendre un café, faire des activités et discuter avec les intervenant·e·s. Dans cette unité mobile d’intervention, aucun sujet n’est tabou. Tu peux parler de tout ce que tu vis de façon confidentielle et anonyme. FAIRE DU TRAVAIL DE RUE À MACADAM SUD POUR LE TROC, EN QUOI ÇA CONSISTE? job_title: Direction générale – Organisme communautaire en sécurité alimentaire
description: La Table ronde de Saint-Léonard est un organisme communautaire engagé dans la lutte contre l’insécurité alimentaire, avec une approche humaine, inclusive et ancrée dans la communauté. Elle offre des services variés visant à répondre aux besoins des personnes en situation de vulnérabilité, tout en favorisant l’autonomie, la dignité et le lien social. Au-delà de l’aide alimentaire, la Table ronde est un véritable lieu de vie et de mobilisation. Votre rôle Relevant du conseil d’administration, la direction générale assure la gestion globale de l’organisme et la mise en œuvre des orientations stratégiques. Elle veille à la cohérence entre la mission, les objectifs et les opérations, tout en assurant une gestion rigoureuse, performante et durable. Nos services Restaurant populaire-Cantine à domicile-Cantine scolaire-Cuisines collectives -Ateliers culinaires Responsabilités principales Leadership et mise en œuvre stratégique Mettre en œuvre les orientations du CA, piloter le plan d’action, assurer l’alignement stratégique et proposer des ajustements en fonction du contexte. Fournir au CA les analyses et informations nécessaires à la prise de décision et Assurer un soutien administratif et logistique aux instances Gestion des opérations Planifier, coordonner et superviser l’ensemble des activités. Assurer la qualité, la pertinence et l’accessibilité des services. Optimiser les processus et assurer la continuité des opérations. Gestion financière et conformité Élaborer et suivre les budgets, assurer une gestion saine des ressources, produire les redditions de comptes, coordonner l’audit et veiller au respect des obligations légales. Développement et financement Développer les sources de financement, coordonner les demandes de subventions, entretenir les relations avec les bailleurs de fonds et assurer la pérennité financière. Gestion des ressources humaines Encadrer, mobiliser et développer une équipe d’environ 15 personnes. Assurer un climat de travail sain et structurer les pratiques RH. Performance et reddition de comptes Mettre en place des indicateurs de performance, produire des rapports au CA et assurer un suivi rigoureux des résultats. Partenariats et représentation Représenter l’organisme, développer les collaborations et contribuer à son rayonnement dans l’écosystème. Gestion des risques Identifier les risques organisationnels et mettre en place des mécanismes de prévention. Profil recherché Exigences Formation universitaire pertinente (administration, gestion ou domaine connexe). Minimum de 3 à 5 ans d’expérience en gestion. Expérience en gestion financière, RH et opérationnelle. Excellente maîtrise du français. Bonne maîtrise des outils informatiques (Suite Office) Atouts : connaissance du communautaire, de Saint Léonard et des enjeux de sécurité alimentaire. Qualités : leadership mobilisateur, rigueur, sens des priorités, capacité d’analyse, intelligence relationnelle et adaptabilité, gestion équipe de 10 personnes ou plus. Conditions de travail Poste permanent (35h/semaine, après probation). Horaire flexible Salaire: entre 65 000 $ et 80 000$ selon l’expérience Avantages 6 semaines de vacances annuelles : – 4 semaines durant la période estivale (fermeture) – 2 semaines durant la période des fêtes 4 journées de congé maladie par année.- Congés fériés. Pourquoi se joindre à nous Contribuer à une mission essentielle. Occuper un rôle structurant et stratégique. Évoluer dans un organisme enraciné dans sa communauté. Avoir un impact concret et mesurable. Postuler Envoyer votre CV et lettre de motivation à : recrutement@tablerondedesaintleonard.ca Date limite : 15 avril Entrée en poste immédiate Seules les personnes retenues seront contactées. Domaine: Administration et gestion 35 heures / semaine Jour, Temps plein Emploi Permanent En présentiel AVANTAGES SOCIAUX Café Conciliation travail-vie personnelles
summary: Ce poste de direction générale supervise l'ensemble des opérations d'un organisme communautaire luttant contre l'insécurité alimentaire, assurant la gestion stratégique, financière, des ressources humaines et le développement pour soutenir l'autonomie et la dignité des personnes vulnérables.

description: COORDINATION AU TRAVAIL DE PROXIMITÉ Poste contractuel pour une durée de six (6 mois) avec possibilité de renouvellement, 35 heures Affichage interne et externe Actif au centre-ville de Montréal depuis 1989, CACTUS Montréal est un organisme communautaire qui a pour mission de réduire la transmission du VIH et autres ITSS auprès des personnes qui consomment des drogues par injection et inhalation, des travailleurs et travailleuses du sexe ainsi que des personnes travesties et transgenres, tout en développant des services spécifiques. La réduction des méfaits guide toutes nos interventions.
