description: Healthy and regenerative, local food systems Position: Director of Programming (Toronto area) Organization: Canadian Centre for Food and Ecology (CCFE) Location: Downtown Toronto ON (primarily on-site, at the CCFE’s homebase at the Centre for Social Innovation, with periodic in-person meetings or events in the Greater Toronto Area.) About the Canadian Centre for Food and Ecology (CCFE): If you are an experienced program leader with a conviction for taste-driven, joyfully immersive programming delivered with and through partnerships to reach targeted audiences, we want to meet you. The Canadian Centre for Food and Ecology (CCFE) is a national charity established in 2024 with a mission to educate and mobilize Canadians in support of a healthy food system that works in harmony with nature. Our aim is to elevate and amplify the voices that are regenerating local food economies. As we embark on a three-year initiative with the primary strategic outcome to develop and pilot a replicable, financially-sustainable, bioregionally-based model that drives food system change from the demand side, we are seeking a Director of Programs to work from our home-base at the Centre for Social Innovation (CSI) and co-create programs that inspire communities in the Greater Tkaronto Bioregion (GTB) to unlock the regenerative potential of our local food economy. Reporting to the Executive Director and serving on the Senior Leadership Team, this role will establish a calendar of taste-driven programs backed by an on-line resource that supports, scales, and tracks shifts in food purchasing behaviour. About the Role: Supported by leading edge audience motivations and insights, communications expertise, and guidelines for behavioural science informed strategies, this role is accountable for developing a vision for CCFE programming, and overseeing all aspects of program design, stakeholder engagement, and program delivery to achieve the organization’s impact goals pertaining to: Food Education: strengthened understanding of the link between how food is grown, health & well-being, and the environment. Food Production: increased market opportunities and equitable collaboration with producer partners. Food Quality: Increased and sustained preferences for regeneratively and locally grown, nutrient-dense foods in partner communities. Food Security: improved year-round access to regeneratively and locally grown, nutrient-dense food. As such, this role is central to advancing the organization’s key three-year strategy to identify, mobilize and equip key stakeholders in the GTB to ideate, test, target, and track impactful, financially-sustainable year-round programming in the bioregion. Key Responsibilities and Duties Strategic Leadership Develop a calendar of new events and programs that are rooted at the CSI and designed to engage audiences in the GTB. Ensure that program designs incorporate insights on the target audience needs and motivations and are based on behavioural science-informed strategies. Establish clear objectives and goals to deliver impactful programs. Work with the Communications team to deliver effective communications plans in support of program goals. With the Executive Director and the Board, incorporate earned revenue and funding goals into program development. Represent Programming in organizational planning, budgeting, best practice guidelines, and resource planning. Program Management and Growth Starting with Flavour Harvest in select Farmers Market this 2026 summer season, build out the growth plan for the Flavour Harvest program brand in Fall 2026 and beyond. Lead and be involved in the day-to-day operations of place-based programs. Oversee the roll-out and further development of a corporate service offering designed to engage people through their place of work. Develop, execute, and evaluate program growth strategies to expand reach and impact while maintaining relational integrity. Team Leadership & Management Identify and assemble the needed resources for the execution of impactful programs. Lead recruitment, professional development, and recognition initiatives within the Programming team. Ensure projects are delivered on time and on budget. Build on and nurture a culture of accountability, collaboration, systems-thinking, entrepreneurship, diversity, and problem-solving. Model equitable collaboration with program partners and cultivate this competency within all team members. Monitoring & Evaluation Ensure program evaluation and the organization’s culture of developmental evaluation are applied toward continuous learning and improvement. Ensure accurate and timely reporting of program outputs and outcomes to the organization’s impact dashboard (internal) and funders (external). Translate program data into actionable insights for continuous improvement. Stakeholder Engagement Lead efforts to co-create programs with partners, including government and foundation stakeholders. Oversee the full participant journey for both ecosystem partners and demand-side participants - from first bite to ongoing engagement. Ensure the organization’s Partnership Principles are followed and reflected in all programs. Represent CCFE at community events, conferences, and sector tables. Qualifications Conviction for CCFE’s mission, vision and values. 8+ years of experience creating programs in related fields, with deep knowledge of food-related programming. At least 5 years of progressive program management leadership, including budgeting, evaluation, and strategic oversight. Exceptional team leadership, communication, coaching, and team‑building skills. Strong understanding of insights-informed design. Experience in nonprofit fundraising, grant writing, and evaluation and impact reporting considered an asset. Ability to thrive in a collaborative, dynamic environment with diverse stakeholders. A strong commitment to equity, inclusion, and community impact. A genuine passion for supporting actors working at the front lines of regenerative local food systems. Compensation This is a full-time position, with a salary range of $100,000-$135,000, commensurate with experience. Work Schedule This position is primarily on-site, at the CCFE’s homebase at the Centre for Social Innovation, with periodic in-person meetings or events in the Greater Toronto Area. Why Join CCFE? Be part of a growing organization shaping the future of sustainable food systems in Canada. Collaborate with a passionate, multidisciplinary team. Work in a flexible, creative, and impact-oriented environment. Gain hands-on experience in nonprofit strategy, development, and ecosystem building. Comprehensive Benefits package including: Health, Dental, Health Care Spending Account, and Life Insurance 3.5 Cultural Days 15 Vacation Days to start Accommodation Prior to the next step in the recruiting process, we welcome you to inform us confidentially if you may require any accommodations in order to participate fully in our recruitment experience. Please contact zahra@theccfe.org to notify us of any needs related to completing the job application and/or throughout the recruitment process. Diversity, Equity & Inclusion The Canadian Centre for Food and Ecology (CCFE) aspires to be an equitable and inclusive place where a diversity of life experiences, identities, and perspectives work together. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds and lived experiences to apply. Application If you’re excited about joining the CCFE team and meet the qualifications, please submit the following as a single PDF: A one-page cover letter outlining your interest in the role and alignment with CCFE’s mission. Your resume. Please write the title of the position in the subject line and save your file as: First Name_Last Name_ProgramDirector.pdf Submit your application to: hello@theccfe.org Please mention you saw this at GoodWork.ca. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.
summary: This Director of Programming leads the development and delivery of taste-driven, joyfully immersive programs to educate and mobilize Canadians in support of a healthy, regenerative, and local food system.

description: Energy management consulting Position: Finance Analyst Company: Goldfin Consulting Inc. Location: Toronto ON / Hybrid About Us Goldfin Consulting helps organizations move from ad hoc energy projects to a strategic, integrated approach to energy management. We build the capabilities needed for people to take actions to address the climate crisis. By combining Strategic Energy Management with intentional workforce development and adult learning principles, Goldfin helps organizations build the skills, systems and culture needed to embed energy performance into everyday business practices. Role Summary Within Goldfin’s growing consulting business, the Finance Analyst is a high-impact and hands-on role, supporting financial planning, performance analysis, and operational decision-making. This role plays a critical part in scaling financial processes, improving visibility into project and company performance, and enabling leadership to make informed strategic decisions. Operating in a lean environment, the Finance Analyst works closely with leadership, project management, and operations to deliver timely insights on revenue, profitability, utilization, and cash flow, while helping build the financial infrastructure required for continued growth. Responsibilities 1. Financial Planning & Analysis Support budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning Track actuals vs. budget and explain variances Develop financial models to support resourcing and compensation planning, pricing, and growth decisions 2. Revenue & Project Profitability Analysis Analyze project-level performance (revenue, margin, utilization) Partner with project management and delivery teams to revise forecasts and/or improve project economics Identify trends in billable hours, rates, realization, and utilization 3. Pricing and Strategic Support Assist with pricing and profitability models for proposals and contract development Provide ad hoc analysis to support business decisions 4. KPI Development & Reporting Build and maintain dashboards for key metrics, such as project and deliverable margins, effective billable rates. Deliver regular reporting packages to leadership 5. Cash Flow & Financial Health Monitoring Maintain cash flow projections, monitor cash position, AR, and billing cycles Help ensure the business scales without cash constraints 6. Process Improvement & Systems Help implement and improve financial systems, tools, and processes Automate reporting and reduce manual work Support integration between finance and project management tools 7. Revenue Operations Ownership and implementation of invoicing activities, ensuring timeliness, accuracy, and compliance with QA/QC procedures and contract terms. Interacting with clients, contractors and vendors to answer questions and resolve issues. 8. Financial Operations Ownership and implementation of internal accounting activities, including managing accounts payable, accounts receivable, reconciling expenses, and tax administration. Liaise with external accountants on payroll, bookkeeping, accounting, tax payments and financial reporting. 9. Banking Operations Manage Goldfin’s banking needs, including managing accounts, credit, and credit cards. Profile / Ideal Candidate 2–5 years of experience in finance, FP&A, consulting, or accounting Strong analytical skills, combined with the ability to apply critical thinking and problem solving to make recommendations or take initiative to implement solutions Experience building models and data tracking and monitoring systems (Excel or equivalent) Experience with project-based or services businesses is a strong asset Comfortable working in a fast-paced, evolving environment Able to translate financial data into actionable business insights Strong communication skills—can work directly with non-finance stakeholders This might be the right role for you if you’re looking for… High visibility: Direct exposure to leadership and strategic decisions Broad scope: Not siloed—touches all aspects of the business Builder role: Opportunity to shape processes, not just follow them Why Work at Goldfin Goldfin was founded with the goal of bringing together a talented team dedicated to doing meaningful work, with a strong commitment to the well-being and fair treatment of our people. We are passionate about our mission to help organizations reduce energy use and GHG emissions to address the climate crisis, and we foster a culture of respect, candor, and continuous learning. Our team is made up of innovative, supportive individuals who value work-life balance and bring their true selves to work. At Goldfin, we collaborate, learn from each other, and are always excited to bring fresh ideas to the table. If you're looking to join an inspiring, driven team, we’d love to have you on board! We offer: 35-hour standard work week 3 weeks of vacation, 10 personal days, plus a 3-day paid-holiday period at the end of the year (i.e. up to 28 days total) 1:1 registered retirement savings plan (RRSP) matching up to 3% of salary Attractive health benefits Hybrid work environment with flexible work hours Home office setup supplies (computer, monitor, mouse, keyboard, headset, and potentially other equipment, on as needed basis) A minimum $2,500 annual personal development budget Proactive salary assessments to ensure fair compensation, stay competitive with market rates, and maintain pay equity across similar roles Bonus: When Goldfin does well, Goldfinners do well – profits are shared with team members Apply Apply here: https://goldfin.ca/careers/ Please mention you saw this at GoodWork.ca.

job_title: Analyste, comptabilité des revenus et intégrité des données
description: Groupe professionnel – permanent Centraide du Grand Montréal est un organisme philanthropique qui soutient plus de 375 organismes et projets communautaires à Laval, à Montréal et sur la Rive-Sud. En vous joignant à notre équipe, vous plongez dans un environnement riche et stimulant au sein duquel les valeurs comme le dépassement, le respect, la collaboration, l’intégrité et la solidarité ont priorité. Relevant de la direction principale, Comptabilité et performance financière, la personne titulaire du poste agit comme référence professionnelle pour l’analyse quotidienne des paiements reçus, la comptabilité des revenus et l’intégrité des données financières entre les différents systèmes (banque, CRM et ERP). Elle joue un rôle central dans la détection, l’investigation et la documentation des flux financiers, particulièrement lorsque les paiements sont non identifiés ou partiellement identifiés, et contribue directement à la fluidité et la qualité des fermetures de mois. La personne titulaire travaille en étroite collaboration avec le contrôleur, les équipes de traitement des dons et l’équipe de l’analyste financier, en assurant la cohérence, la rigueur et la fiabilité des données utilisées pour la reddition de comptes et la performance financière. RESPONSABILITÉS PRINCIPALES Analyser quotidiennement les paiements reçus dans les comptes bancaires; Répertorier les paiements non identifiés ou partiellement identifiés et effectuer les suivis requis; Effectuer des investigations croisées entre l’information bancaire, le CRM (Salesforce), l’historique des dons et les engagements existants; Déterminer et documenter la logique d’allocation des paiements (fonds, segments, projets, campagnes, items); Documenter ses analyses de façon structurée, traçable et auditable (hypothèses, références, impacts financiers); Transmettre des instructions claires et documentées au groupe de traitement des dons pour l’application des paiements dans le CRM. Précision : la personne titulaire n’effectue pas elle-même les transactions dans le CRM. Elle analyse, sécurise et documente la logique, et le traitement des dons exécute les transactions. Assurer le processus complet de conciliation mensuelle des revenus, encaissements et engagements; Analyser et expliquer les écarts par fonds, segments, projets, campagnes et périodes; Préparer, documenter et valider les écritures comptables liées aux revenus reportés, créances et ajustements; Contribuer activement à la fermeture de mois, dans le respect des échéanciers; Soutenir le contrôleur dans l’analyse des impacts financiers et la qualité de l’information produite. Assurer la cohérence et la fiabilité des données entre la banque, le CRM, l’ERP (Business Central) et les rapports financiers; Identifier les anomalies systémiques ou bris de processus et en documenter les causes; Contribuer à l’amélioration continue des processus liés aux flux de revenus et aux contrôles opérationnels; Agir comme personne-ressource pour les enjeux de qualité des données financières. Produire des analyses détaillées à partir de données volumineuses (Excel avancé : recherches, tableaux croisés, analyses); Collaborer avec l’analyste financier pour assurer la fiabilité des données utilisées pour le budget, la reddition de comptes et les analyses de performance; Soutenir les équipes internes dans la compréhension des écarts et des impacts financiers; Contribuer, au besoin, aux processus d’audit interne. Accomplit temporairement les tâches d’un poste connexe ou inférieur, lorsque requis. La liste des tâches et responsabilités ci-dessus énumérées est sommaire et indicative. Il ne s’agit pas d’une liste complète et détaillée des tâches et responsabilités susceptibles d’être effectuées par le titulaire de ce poste. Cependant, les tâches et responsabilités non énumérées ne doivent pas avoir d’effet sur l’évaluation de l’emploi. PROFIL REQUIS Scolarité et expérience Être titulaire d’un Baccalauréat en comptabilité ou finance; Avoir un minimum de 3 à 5 ans d’expérience en comptabilité financière, analyse ou audit; Être membre en règle de l’Ordre CPA ou en voie de l’obtenir (un atout). Compétences spécifiques Maîtrise des logiciels de la Suite MS Office (Excel avancé, Outlook, SharePoint, Teams, Word,Powerpoint, OneNote); Très bonnes habilités avec les outils informatiques suivants: D365 Business Central; Power Query et Power BI; CRM SalesForce, un atout; Excellente maîtrise du français tant à l’oral qu’à l’écrit; Maîtrise de l’anglais nécessaire pour interagir avec des partenaires anglophones; Excellente capacité d’analyse, d’investigation et de jugement comptable; Capacité à gérer simultanément les enjeux quotidiens et les échéances des fermetures mensuelles; Rigueur, autonomie, et souci élevé de la qualité des données; Habileté à traiter de l’information d’une façon éthique, rigoureuse et confidentielle. Compétences transversales Capacité d’adaptation : Être en mesure d’adopter une attitude positive et confiante face aux changements et à l’incertitude ; Communication : Articuler de manière constructive et bienveillante des idées, concepts et points de vue personnels tout en cherchant à comprendre le point de vue des autres ; Agir de manière responsable : Accepter des responsabilités, assumer les conséquences de ses décisions et inspirer confiance aux autres par ses actions ; Être innovant : Capacité à développer, exprimer et appliquer des nouvelles idées et de remettre en question les méthodes et normes existantes ; Collaboration et entraide : Travailler en collaboration en démontrant du respect pour les différences individuelles et soutenir les autres pour atteindre un objectif commun. Incarner et promouvoir les valeurs de Centraide: Solidarité, respect, dépassement, collaboration et intégrité. CE QUE NOUS OFFRONS À Centraide, l’humain est au cœur de nos priorités. Voici quelques avantages à travailler parmi nous : Mode de travail hybride (présentiel et télétravail); Horaire flexible de 35 heures; Horaire réduit l’été; Équipe dynamique et bienveillante; Conciliation travail/famille valorisée; Possibilité d’évolution de carrière; Remboursement d’activité de formation et de perfectionnement; Télémédecine et programme d’aide aux employés; Assurances collectives; Régime de retraite. (Très) en faveur de la diversité Centraide applique un programme d’accès à l’égalité pour des groupes susceptibles de vivre de la discrimination en emploi c’est à dire les membres de minorités visibles et ethniques, les personnes en situation de handicap, les Autochtones et les femmes. Postuler ici Nous remercions toutes les personnes qui poseront leur candidature, mais nous communiquerons qu’avec celles retenues pour un processus de sélection.
summary: Ce rôle d'analyste assure l'intégrité et la fiabilité des données financières de Centraide, en analysant les paiements, répertoriant les fonds et contribuant aux fermetures de mois pour un organisme philanthropique.

organization: Association des intervenants en dépendance du Québec
description: L’Association des intervenants en dépendance du Québec a pour mission de valoriser la pratique et de soutenir l’intervention en prévention, réduction des méfaits, traitement et réinsertion sociale relativement à l’usage de substances psychoactives, le jeu de hasard et d’argent ainsi que l’utilisation d’Internet et des écrans. description: Apprentice Positions 2026 Apply Now for 2026 Farm Apprenticeships! Positions: Farm Apprenticeships 2026 Organization: SOIL Apprenticeships Location: many locations across Canada Are you self-motivated, eager to take a peek into the farming world and unsure where to start? SOIL Apprenticeships offers a connection between aspiring farmers and small farmers across Canada. The host farms that list with SOIL, all Canadian, represent a wide variety of focus and practices. You could choose to work with farmers producing nutritious food for a market garden operation, discover the enormous potential of growing healthy vegetables in raised beds, using natural fertilizers, biological pest control and more. Perhaps you might learn the basics of animal husbandry while apprenticing on a small dairy farm or on the expanse of a large cattle ranch. Experience first-hand the advantages that can be gained by working with draft horses or developing the knowledge and skills necessary to properly care for fruit trees. The opportunities are endless. This program was initiated to encourage the growth of sustainable agriculture. For this reason, SOIL is only offered to farms which emphasize organic techniques with little or no dependence on pesticides, herbicides, or fungicides. A time commitment of eight weeks is usually required. A full-season commitment is usually preferred. Most apprenticeships involve labor in exchange for room, board and the opportunity to learn, although some farms provide a wage or small allowance. Farms must make a commitment to provide a teaching component to the apprenticeship. They are encouraged to provide a monthly stipend or wage to the apprentice. If this is not practical, most apprentices agree to room & board and a productive learning experience in return for their labor. SOIL acts as a liaison between the farmer and the apprentice. Typically, apprenticeships take place between May and September, although many farms need help all year round. We endeavour to match the apprentice with the farm according to the information given by both parties. It is the responsibility of both parties to come to a working agreement. Both parties should discuss such topics as length of commitment, hours of work, learning outcomes expected, housing and food arrangements, holidays, sick days, insurance, and other special needs. description: Web application development Position: Web Application Developer Organization: Birds Canada Location: This role may be performed remotely from anywhere in Canada or from one of our office locations (Port Rowan, ON, or Sackville, NB). Birds Canada’s Data Science and Technology branch maintains two internationally recognized conservation technology platforms NatureCounts (naturecounts.ca) and the Motus Wildlife Tracking System (motus.org). These tools support hundreds of research and monitoring projects across more than 400 institutions, enabling the collection, management, and sharing of thousands of datasets representing nearly 10 billion observations. These data have contributed to more than 4,500 scientific publications. These data and tools are instrumental to the successful implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and Canada’s 2030 Nature Strategy, and for solving applied conservation challenges from local to global scales (see Evidence of Success and this video). We also offer a primarily employer-paid extended health and dental benefits package - including disability, life insurance, vision care, travel insurance, and an Employee/Family Assistance Plan, as well as access to exclusive employee discounts through select outdoor and conservation-focused partners. Birds Canada consistently sees strong employee wellness outcomes and high Employee Net Promoter Scores, reflecting a workplace where people feel supported, engaged, and proud of the work they do. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES The developer, in conjunction with Data Science & Technology staff, may take part in any of the following tasks: Develop responsive, web-based data visualization and exploration tools, including interactive maps, tables and graphs. Optimize performance and speed of data visualization and download tools. Manage workflows and code versioning through git and GitHub. Maintain appropriate documentation on applications. Ensure applications maintain appropriate levels of security and cybersecurity. EDUCATION BSc or technical degree in computer sciences, or a BSc in life sciences, with pertinent experience in web application development. English mandatory, French and/or Spanish would be assets. Working with and optimizing large datasets would be an asset. description:
Company: Zest Digital Marketing

Industry: Digital Advertising & Performance Marketing

Employment Type: Full-Time & Freelancer

I. About Zest Digital Marketing

Zest Digital Marketing is a results-driven digital advertising agency specializing in performance marketing and scalable growth strategies. We partner with brands to deliver measurable impact through data-led campaigns across paid media, social platforms, and digital ecosystems. Our mission is to help businesses accelerate growth through strategic execution and continuous optimization.

II. Position Overview

We are seeking a highly analytical and performance-oriented Performance Marketing Specialist to manage, optimize, and scale paid advertising campaigns across Google Ads and Meta (Facebook & Instagram) platforms.

This role is instrumental in driving qualified leads, customer acquisition, and revenue growth through strategic planning, hands-on execution, and continuous performance optimization.

  • Plan, execute, and manage paid media campaigns across Google Ads (Search, Display, YouTube, Performance Max) and Meta Ads platforms.

  • Monitor, analyze, and optimize campaigns to achieve KPIs such as CPA, ROAS, CTR, CPC, and conversion rate.
  • Collaborate with creative and content teams to develop and test high-performing ad creatives and messaging.
  • Allocate and manage advertising budgets effectively to maximize ROI and scale winning campaigns.
  • Implement and maintain accurate tracking systems using Google Analytics (GA4), Google Tag Manager, Meta Pixel, and conversion tracking tools.
  • Prepare weekly and monthly performance reports, providing actionable insights and optimization recommendations.
  • Stay up to date with industry trends, platform updates, and emerging performance marketing best practices.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally to align paid media strategies with overall marketing and business objectives.

IV. Qualifications & Requirements

  • 1–3+ years of hands-on experience in Paid Media or Digital Advertising.

  • Strong analytical skills with a data-driven decision-making approach.
  • Experience with performance tracking, reporting, and analytics tools.
  • Ability to manage multiple campaigns simultaneously and meet deadlines.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

V. Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in lead generation and/or e-commerce performance campaigns.
  • Knowledge of A/B testing methodologies, remarketing strategies, and funnel optimization.
  • Experience managing medium to large advertising budgets.

VI. What We Offer

  • Competitive salary with performance-based incentives.
  • Opportunity to work with diverse industries and growing brands.
  • Dynamic and fast-paced performance marketing environment.
  • Continuous learning and professional development opportunities.
  • Clear career progression pathways.

VII. How to Apply

Please submit your CV to: hrm@zestdigitalmarketing.com

description: La Coalition montréalaise des Tables de quartier (CMTQ) regroupe 32 tables de concertation locale en développement social. La CMTQ offre un espace d’échange, de partage d’analyses et de soutien à ses membres et les représente dans plusieurs lieux. La CMTQ intervient aussi à l’échelle montréalaise sur des enjeux sociaux et des politiques publiques, dans l’optique d’améliorer les conditions de vie de la population. LE POSTE QUE NOUS OFFRONS : Sous la supervision de la direction générale et en collaboration avec la personne responsable du soutien aux membres, la personne retenue aura comme principal mandat d’assurer la liaison avec les membres et entre les membres, de répondre aux besoins identifiés, de soutenir les directions et les équipes des Tables de quartier dans le renforcement des capacités, d’organiser des activités d’échange sur les pratiques et les enjeux et de faciliter l’implication des membres. LES CONDITIONS DE TRAVAIL QUE NOUS PROPOSONS : Durée du contrat : Poste pour une année avec possibilité de renouvèlement (à confirmer) Horaire : 35 heures/semaine Salaire : selon l’échelle salariale et l’expérience, à partir de 31,61 $/heure Vacances : 4 semaines dès la première année, arrêt des activités 2 semaines durant la période des fêtes Régime de retraite et assurance collective Environnement de travail soucieux de la conciliation travail/famille et du bien-être des personnes. Bureau situé au 3600 rue Bélanger. Possibilité de télétravail à temps partiel. VOS RESPONSABILITÉS La personne titulaire est plus spécifiquement appelée à : Développer et maintenir des liens étroits avec les membres; Développer des stratégies de soutien des membres (direction, équipe, CA des Tables) et de communication entre les membres; Poursuivre les moyens déjà mis en place en soutien aux membres, en collaboration avec la responsable du soutien aux membres et le reste de l’équipe : aide individuelle, soutien collectif, référencement, mentorat, activités de réseautage, communautés de pratiques, partage d’outils, comités et espaces d’échanges sur des enjeux sociaux, etc. Développer de nouvelles façons de renforcer les capacités d’action des Tables de quartier; Participer à la documentation des impacts du réseau des Tables de quartier à Montréal. En lien avec son poste, la personne aura également à participer à l’atteinte de la mission de l’organisme : Prendre en charge un dossier, un projet ou une représentation sur d’autres priorités qui ne sont pas directement reliées au libellé de l’emploi; Contribuer au développement de la vision de l’organisme et à la mise en œuvre du plan d’action; Participer à la vie associative de l’organisme et à l’organisation des assemblées générales, des rencontres thématiques, des comités de travail, des grands événements; Contribuer à la production du rapport d’activités, du plan d’action, des outils de communication et au rayonnement de l’organisme; Participer activement aux réunions d’équipe. La personne titulaire du poste peut également être appelée à réaliser des tâches ou projets connexes. La CMTQ privilégie l’agilité et la souplesse dans l’organisation du travail et favorise le travail en collégialité avec d’autres membres de l’équipe. NOUS RECHERCHONS UNE PERSONNE : Une personne polyvalente, curieuse et autonome, prête à prendre en charge des dossiers variés dans un contexte en constante évolution; Qui aime travailler dans la bonne humeur et le respect et qui a un bon esprit d’équipe; Qui souhaite proposer de nouvelles perspectives; Qui est en mesure de contribuer au développement de son poste; Qui est animé·e par le désir de contribuer à l’amélioration des conditions de vie de la population montréalaise en faisant de Montréal une ville plus juste et plus inclusive. ET QUI POSSEDENT LES QUALIFICATIONS SUIVANTES : Une formation universitaire pertinente; Deux (2) ans d’expérience de travail pertinente; Une bonne connaissance des Tables de quartier ou de la concertation intersectorielle territoriale est un précieux atout; Une expérience en ressources humaines, en gestion ou gouvernance d’organisation est un atout; Avoir un intérêt pour les enjeux sociaux montréalais; Une bonne capacité d’analyse, de communication, de vulgarisation et de mobilisation; Maîtriser le français, tant à l’oral et qu’à l’écrit; Être confortable avec l’utilisation de matériel informatique et logiciels, notamment la suite Microsoft, Zoom, Doodle, Survey Monkey et autre. Domaine: Administration et gestion 35 heures / semaine Temps plein Emploi Permanent Hybride
summary: L'Agent.e de développement assure la liaison et le soutien aux 32 tables de concertation locale en développement social membres de la CMTQ, renforçant leurs capacités et facilitant leur implication pour améliorer les conditions de vie de la population montréalaise.

description: Depuis 1960, Compagnons de Montréal crée des milieux de vie, d’apprentissage et d’inclusion stimulants pour des adultes qui vivent avec une différence intellectuelle ou un trouble du spectre de l’autisme dans une approche de valorisation et d’autonomisation des personnes. Ici, les équipes accompagnent des parcours, encouragent les apprentissages et soutiennent l’émergence du potentiel de chacun. Le service de formation socioprofessionnelle accueille une trentaine de personnes apprenantes qui développent des compétences personnelles, sociales et professionnelles dans différents espaces d’apprentissage : cuisine, entretien ménager, ressources matérielles, vente au détail et agriculture urbaine. SOMMAIRE DU POSTE En étroite collaboration avec la direction et les responsables de service, la personne à la coordination du programme de formation socioprofessionnelle veille à la cohérence, à l’organisation et à la qualité du parcours de formation offert aux personnes apprenantes. Elle soutient les équipes dans la mise en oeuvre du projet pédagogique, assure le suivi du programme et des redditions tout en maintenant les liens avec les partenaires impliqués. Par son rôle, elle contribue à offrir un environnement d’apprentissage structuré, inclusif et stimulant qui favorise le développement des compétences et la participation sociale des personnes accompagnées. RESPONSABILITÉS Coordination du programme socioprofessionnel • Assurer la cohérence et le développement du programme de formation socioprofessionnelle ; • Veiller à l’harmonisation des outils, des stratégies et des objectifs dans les différents espaces de formation ; • Assurer le suivi et l’évaluation du projet pédagogique ; • Coordonner les ressources du service afin de soutenir un parcours de formation structuré et adapté ; • Assurer le recrutement, l’accueil et le suivi des personnes inscrites au programme ; • Assurer un suivi de transition lorsque les personnes quittent le programme. Gestion administrative et organisationnelle • Assurer un suivi administratif rigoureux du programme et des dossiers des participants ; • Maintenir les liens administratifs avec les partenaires institutionnels ; • Participer à la planification et à l’organisation du service ; • Contribuer à la mise en place d’outils de suivi et d’évaluation du programme. Gestion d’équipe • Superviser et accompagner le personnel sous sa responsabilité dans le respect des valeurs et des politiques de l’organisme ; • Participer au recrutement et à l’accueil des nouveaux membres de l’équipe ; • Soutenir, former et évaluer le personnel dans l’accomplissement de leur travail ; • Planifier les horaires de travail et assurer leur suivi ; • Animer des rencontres d’équipe et favoriser la collaboration entre les services. Partenariats et développement • Assurer le suivi des ententes et des collaborations liées au programme de formation socioprofessionnelle ; • Préparer les redditions de comptes et les documents de suivi requis par les partenaires et bailleurs de fond ; • Maintenir des liens de collaboration avec les partenaires du programme, notamment les partenaires pédagogiques et les acteurs du milieu de l’employabilité ; • Identifier, développer et entretenir de nouveaux partenariats, notamment avec des entreprises susceptibles d’offrir des opportunités d’apprentissage, de stage ou d’emploi pour les apprenants ; • Contribuer au développement et au rayonnement du programme de formation socioprofessionnelle ; • Représenter l’organisme dans certains espaces de concertation ou événements liés à l’insertion socioprofessionnelle. Participation à la vie organisationnelle • Participer activement au comité de gestion de l’organisme ; • Contribuer aux réflexions organisationnelles liées au développement des services ; • Réaliser toute autre tâche connexe liée à sa fonction. PROFIL RECHERCHÉ Compétences professionnelles • Formation en travail social, éducation spécialisée, sciences sociales ou domaine connexe • Expérience en insertion socioprofessionnelle, en intervention ou en coordination de service et projets • Expérience en gestion et supervision d’équipe • Connaissance des réalités DI/TSA (atout majeur) • Bonne maîtrise du français à l’écrit et l’oral • Bonne connaissance de la suite Office • Capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités et à structurer des processus. Compétences personnelles • Leadership rassembleur • Sens aigu de l’organisation et des priorités • Sens de l’écoute et posture bienveillante • Capacité d’adaptation et créativité • Diplomatie et écoute active • Sensibilité aux réalités des personnes accompagnées TOI… ✓ Tu es une personne organisée, humaine et mobilisatrice. ✓ Tu aimes travailler en collaboration et soutenir le développement des personnes et des équipes ✓ Tu sais créer un climat de confiance. ✓ Tu vois les différences comme des richesses et tu crois que l’inclusion se construit par l’action concrète. ✓ Tu es capable de gérer plusieurs dossiers à la fois sans perdre le sens du projet. ✓ Tu es à l’aise dans un rôle où la coordination, l’humain et la structure doivent coexister au quotidien. NOUS… Faire partie de notre équipe c’est : ✓ Un taux horaire à 25 $ ; ✓ Trois semaines de vacances dès la première année complétée + 1 semaine au temps des Fêtes ; ✓ Des congés personnels ; ✓ Une assurance collective dont 50 % sont défrayés par nous ; ✓ Contribuer tous les jours à une mission stimulante et essentielle ; ✓ Évoluer dans un environnement de travail sympathique, bienveillant et flexible ; ✓ Travailler aux côtés d’une équipe engagée et compétente, dédiée à la cause ; + Quelques autres petites douceurs qui font une grande différence et sont uniques à Compagnons. description: Prévention du Crime Ahuntsic-Cartierville (PCAC) est un organisme communautaire engagé dans la promotion du sentiment de sécurité, la cohabitation harmonieuse et du vivre ensemble au sein de l’arrondissement Ahuntsic-Cartierville. Depuis plusieurs années, notre équipe développe et adapte ses actions afin de répondre aux enjeux émergents du territoire et aux besoins des citoyens. Pour renforcer le sentiment de sécurité et favoriser des milieux de vie inclusifs, nous allons directement à la rencontre des résidents dans l’ensemble de nos interventions. Nous offrons notamment des ateliers de sensibilisation portant sur des thèmes variés tels que le harcèlement de rue, la fraude ou les déplacements sécuritaires. Nous organisons également des activités favorisant la cohabitation et la participation citoyenne, afin de briser l’isolement social et créer des espaces de rencontre. Notre organisme contribue aussi à l’embellissement du quartier en procédant au retrait des graffitis et en réalisant des murales communautaires. Durant la période estivale, nous accueillons une équipe de jeunes qui patrouille dans les parcs et sur les pistes cyclables pour informer, sensibiliser et soutenir les citoyens. Enfin, notre équipe est formée en médiation sociale et intervient auprès des résidents pour les accompagner dans la résolution de conflits de voisinage, toujours dans une approche constructive et respectueuse. Si la sécurité urbaine pour la jeunesse vous tient à coeur, vous êtes à la bonne place! Description du poste Sous la supervision de la directrice de l’organisme, vous aurez le mandat de mettre en oeuvre le projet graffiti. Ce projet communautaire vise à assurer la sécurité en embellissant les espaces publics à travers une présence et des actions préventives. Vous participerez activement à répondre aux demandes des citoyen.ne.s ainsi que de l’arrondissement d’Ahuntsic-Cartierville. Vous superviserez une équipe d’employés durant la période estivale. Description des tâches – Gérer les appels d’offres pour le contrat d’enlèvement de graffitis. – Traiter les demandes citoyennes et les signalements transmis par l’arrondissement (service 311). – Travailler en collaboration avec divers partenaires. – Recenser les graffitis sur le domaine privé et public d’Ahuntsic‑Cartierville. – Mettre à jour la banque de données (photos, interventions, statistiques). – Planifier et coordonner les opérations de retrait sur le territoire. – Superviser l’équipe terrain chargée du nettoyage. – Tenir à jour le tableau Excel des interventions. – Rédiger deux rapports d’étape et un rapport annuel. – Développer des stratégies de prévention et de sensibilisation auprès des jeunes et de la communauté Formation – Avoir un diplôme d’études collégiales (DEC) ou universitaires en intervention, travail social, criminologie, animation, gestion de projets ou domaine connexe. – Toute combinaison de formation et d’expérience pertinente sera considérée. Compétences et qualités recherchées – Excellentes capacités d’organisation, de planification et de coordination. – Aisance à superviser une équipe terrain et à travailler en collaboration avec divers partenaires. – Rigueur dans la gestion de données, la tenue de registres et la rédaction de rapports. – Bonne maitrise des outils informatiques, notamment Excel et la gestion de bases de données. – Sens de l’initiative et capacité à développer des stratégies de prévention et de sensibilisation. – Bonne communication orale et écrite, tact et diplomatie dans les relations avec les citoyens et l’arrondissement. – Intérêt pour les enjeux de sécurité urbaine, de prévention et d’engagement communautaire. Conditions de travail – Poste à temps plein de avril à décembre puis temps partiel de janvier à mars (horaire flexible) – Horaire de jour, avec possibilité d’activités en soirée ou fin de semaine selon les besoins du projet. – Contrat annuel renouvelable, sous réserve du financement. – Salaire : 25$/heure – Lieu de travail : arrondissement Ahuntsic‐Cartierville, avec déplacements sur le territoire pour les opérations terrain. – Entrée en fonction : 1er avril Avantages – Frais de déplacement et de cellulaire remboursés – Possibilité d’avoir accès à Communauto pour les déplacements terrain – Environnement de travail collaboratif, axé sur la prévention, la sécurité urbaine et l’engagement citoyen. – Un poste qui offre la possibilité de travailler à l’extérieur, favorisant variété et bienêtre. WHAT WILL YOU DO?
The Shared Services Technician is part of the Technical Resources Group and Technical Field Activities Team who supports project teams and works under the direction of more senior staff. The role focuses on data collection, inspection, equipment maintenance, and preparation of technical documentation to support service line teams in both field and office environments. Tasks can vary within service groups and based on project type, as detailed below.

JOB DUTIES

  • Conduct standard fieldwork including sample collection, basic testing, inspections, and monitoring in accordance with established procedures and protocols.

  • Operate, calibrate, maintain, and safely use field monitoring and sampling equipment.

  • Support abatement, remediation, and construction projects through routine inspection and testing to verify compliance with applicable guidelines and regulations.
  • Assist with data compilation and contribute to report preparation by providing accurate field data and observations.
  • Follow standard operating procedures, best management practices, and applicable health, safety, and environmental requirements.
  • Communicate effectively with project team members regarding field activities, observations, and issues encountered.
  • Maintain field equipment, track supplies, and report equipment or material needs to senior staff.
  • Complete timesheets and expense submissions accurately and within required deadlines.
  • Perform work in accordance with professional conduct, ethical standards, and organizational policies.
  • Take reasonable care for personal safety and the safety of others by using required personal protective equipment, reporting hazards or incidents, and maintaining a clean and organized work area.


QUALIFICATIONS

  • Undergraduate degree or college diploma in a related discipline such as science or engineering
  • 0-1+ years of relevant experience
  • Knowledge of related legislation and regulations
  • Ability to learn about several service lines and related responsibilities quickly and apply new knowledge, with a drive to succeed
  • Good problem-solving and critical thinking skills
  • Good organizational skills with attention to detail
  • Good communication skills with the ability to listen and clarify
  • Good computer skills, with proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, TEAMS, and other project-related software and databases
  • Ability to work independently, while also being able to collaborate as part of a team
  • Good interpersonal skills with the ability build positive relationships with team and contractors
  • Good customer service orientation
  • Flexible and adaptable to changing needs
  • A high level of integrity, ability to maintain confidentiality, and pride in quality work
  • Valid driver’s license and access to a reliable vehicle
  • The successful candidate will demonstrate excellent communication skills with fluency (reading, writing and oral) in English.

description: Sustainable Business, Supply Chain Sustainability Position: Senior Commercial Manager, Canada Organization: Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) Location: Toronto ON / Hybrid Would you like to work for a global nonprofit committed to the preservation of the oceans? If so, this could be the opportunity for you! The MSC Canada team is currently looking to recruit a Senior Commercial Manager to join the team. As a Senior Commercial Manager, you’ll have the opportunity to lead on the implementation of MSC's commercial strategy in Canada and to help deliver the MSC’s overall goals. This is a senior position, and the post holder will lead Canada’s commercial strategy with its aim to increase the availability of MSC-certified and labelled products for consumers. Successful commercial outreach lies at the core of the MSC program and plays a crucial role in driving participation in the program. In this position, you will be responsible for promoting MSC certification and establishing connections with retailers, and seafood businesses. Your goal will be to encourage sustainability and certification, ultimately safeguarding our oceans. To be successful in this role, besides sharing our enthusiasm for our oceans, our ideal candidate will also have the following key skills / experience: Post-graduate degree or equivalent experience in Business, Supply Chain Sustainability or Resource Management Extensive experience leading, developing and delivering integrated commercial strategies Ideally some experience working in, or with, the Canada seafood sector or an environmental organisation Extensive knowledge of the seafood industry, with existing contacts and networks highly desirable Previous line management experience an asset Fluency in both spoken and written English. If this has inspired you, please apply on msc.org! Please mention you saw this at GoodWork.ca. We look forward to hearing from you! We’re an international organisation and our employees all demonstrate a level of cultural awareness, and value the diverse views and approaches relevant to the MSC program. The MSC is committed to flexible working. The successful candidate will need to work from the Toronto office for a minimum of 50% of their working time each month The remaining time can be worked from home. During the onboarding process, hybrid work may require more in-office work than remote work. Please be aware, we are only able to progress with candidates who already have the right to work in the location(s) specified in this advert. Unfortunately, we are not able to offer visa sponsorship at this time. The MSC’s vision is for the world’s oceans to be teeming with life, and seafood supplies safeguarded for this and future generations. Through our internationally recognised certification and ecolabeling program, well-managed sustainable fisheries are recognised and rewarded in the marketplace, through the leadership of our partners. Over 400 fisheries around the world, representing more than 17% of the annual global marine catch, are now engaged in the MSC program and MSC certified and labelled seafood products are now available in over 100 countries. The MSC is committed to the principles of equality and fairness and we welcome applications from all communities. We do not discriminate on the grounds of age, ethnicity, race, colour, religion or belief, gender or gender identity, sexual orientation or disability. If you consider yourself to have a disability and need reasonable adjustments made during the recruitment and selection process, please let us know how we can help you.

description: Summer jobs, Student jobs Position: Wildlife Biologist (Avian Field Assistant- youth) Type: age 30 & under / summer Organization: Pelee Island Bird Observatory Location: Pelee Island, Ontario Housing: free housing, but food and transportation to and from the island is the responsibility of the candidate Anticipated start date: May 4 2026 * dates somewhat flexible Anticipated end date: June 29, 2026 Duration: 8 weeks Hourly wage: $ 20.00/hour for 35 hours a week The Pelee Island Bird Observatory (PIBO) is a regional not-for-profit organization dedicated to the conservation of birds by conducting scientific research, avian population monitoring, and connecting people to nature. The field station and its work are done on Pelee Island, which sits in the migratory path of two major North American flyways, a premier location to study and observe hundreds of migratory species and dozens of breeding birds with limited ranges in Canada. We are looking for an enthusiastic environmentalist to join our team as Avian Field Assistant for the spring and early summer seasons (May 4 through June 29) at our field station on Pelee Island, near Windsor, Ontario. As Avian Field Assistant you will report to the Field Supervisor and be responsible for helping with the spring and early summer research, data management, field station logistics and maintenance, as well as assisting in the delivery of on-island education programs (as needed). Depending upon experience, your duties include: FIELDWORK DUTIES daily constant-effort migration-monitoring, including assisting with daily 90 minute census passerine bird banding in May summer breeding bird studies species-at-risk monitoring marsh bird and amphibian surveys additional spring and summer research activities (as required) RECORD-KEEPING DUTIES Entry and proofing of research data collected during the season including PIBO’s Daily Totals (DTs), bird banding records, species-a-risk data, marsh bird surveys, amphibian monitoring, etc. Assist with online social media updates during the spring migration season, and contribute articles to the newsletter, as required. OTHER DUTIES Assist with equipment and vehicle upkeep, and staff house maintenance (includes shopping, cooking, cleaning, etc.). Qualifications/Requirements: Some songbird banding and extraction experience Familiar with birds of the Great Lakes region Comfortable interacting with the public Data entry and proofing, and be familiar with at least excel data entry Assist with the upkeep of the PIBO staff cottage and field station, help with shopping, cleaning, etc. Assist with PIBO island education programs and events- banding demonstrations, etc. Conditions around the banding station are sometimes flooded and often muddy. You must be able to spend long periods standing and walking over uneven terrain. Candidates should bring their own field gear- rubber boots, mosquito hats/shirts, and clothing for warm and cold weather, etc. Hip waders are useful as well. Driver’s license is not essential but helpful. Must be an early-riser! Work starts almost every day before dawn. Must be mature, dependable and easy to live with. Perks/Conditions: Candidate will be provided with free housing but food and transportation to and from the island is the responsibility of the candidate. This position is contingent upon funding from Canada Summer Jobs. We are looking for a recent graduate (last 3 years) in the fields of biology, zoology or ornithology. Applicants must be under the age of 30 at the start of employment. Must be legally entitled to work in Ontario. This includes frequent travel to key markets to attend meetings and events. The Senior Development Officer, Partnerships is responsible for developing a national cultivation strategy, which includes planning the logistics and managing a budget to execute this strategy. The Senior Development Officer, Partnerships is a senior development professional with a proven track record of identifying, cultivating, and closing major and transformational corporate philanthropic and sponsorship commitments. The Senior Development Officer, Partnerships is an ambassador for the Wilder Institute and Wilder Institute/Calgary Zoo to all external audiences. They excel at inspiring others to join us on our journey to restore the balance between wildlife and wild places. Our Purpose | We act for wildlife; saving species and inspiring people to join us. Our Core Values | Drive impact, nurture connection, cultivate hope, and be bold. description: Le Centre de services scolaire de Montréal (CSSDM) est le plus important employeur dans le monde de l’éducation au Québec et l’un des plus importants de la région métropolitaine. Son mandat est d’organiser les services éducatifs dans les établissements d’enseignement préscolaire, primaire, secondaire, les écoles spécialisées pour les élèves handicapés ou en difficulté d’adaptation ou d’apprentissage (EHDAA), les écoles de formation professionnelle et les centres d’éducation des adultes. Une équipe de 18000employés, dont 8000 enseignants, mettent leurs compétences à profit pour assurer les services éducatifs auprès de 114000 élèves, jeunes et adultes. Vous souhaitez en apprendre davantage sur le quotidien de nos employés? Lisez lestémoignages de nos ambassadeurs! LeCSSDM recherche des secrétaires et agentes ou agents de bureau afin d’intégrer sa liste de rappel pour effectuerdes remplacements à court et à long terme afin de contribuer activement à la réussite de TOUS ses élèves. Être secrétaire ou agent(e) de bureau au CSSDM, c’est… Travailler au sein du plus grand réseau d’écoles de la métropole, accessible en transport en commun Avoir la possibilité de choisir votre secteur géographique dans le territoire du CSSDM Accéder à des formations permettant le développement professionnel, selon l’emploi occupé Avoir une conciliation entre le travail et sa vie personnelle: occuper un emploi de jour, du lundi au vendredi, adapté à vos disponibilités Possibilité d’horaire réduit (semaine de relâche et semaines déterminées pendant la période estivale) * Bénéficier des avantages sociaux de la fonction publique (fonds de pension à prestations déterminées, assurances collectives, vacances, etc.) * Possibilité de bénéficier de 4 semaines de vacances, après seulement une première année à l’emploi du CSSDM* Bénéficier de rabais corporatifs pour les employés (activités physiques, santé et bien-être, activités sociales, transport, assurances, téléphonie, lunetterie, informatique) *des conditions liées à la convention collective s’appliquent. Le Centre de services scolaire de Montréal (CSSDM) est le plus important employeur dans le monde de l’éducation au Québec et l’un des plus importants de la région métropolitaine, consulter la carte des territoires. Rôle et responsabilités Accueille les visiteurs et assure le service à la clientèle avec les parents et les élèves; Effectue la saisie de textes, de données et de tableaux à l’ordinateur; Corrige des textes; Traite les appels téléphoniques et fournit des renseignements généraux; Tient à jour les dossiers et registres des classes; Traite le courrier postal et les courriels; Collige les données nécessaires pour la préparation du budget, participe à son élaboration, voit à son suivi et dresse des rapports sur les soldes budgétaires; Effectue la tenue des livres comptables de l’établissement et s’assure d’effectuer certains paiements. Qualifications requises* Correspondre à l’un des quatre profils suivants: Être titulaire d’un diplôme d’études professionnelles (DEP) en secrétariat Être titulaire d’un diplôme d’études collégiales (DEC) en techniques de bureautique, option coordination de travail de bureau Être titulaire d’une attestation d’études collégiales (AEC) en bureautique** en bureautique-d’agent d’administration en coordination de travail de bureau Être titulaire d’un diplôme d’études secondaires (DES) ou d’une attestation d’équivalence de niveau secondaire (AENS). Posséder de l’expérience en secrétariat est un atout. *Veuillez noter que pour les diplômes obtenus à l’étranger, afin de valider adéquatement les qualifications requises, l’évaluation comparative de vos études effectuées hors Québec est impérative et doit être obtenue au moment de postuler. Celle-ci est délivrée par le ministère de l’Immigration, de la Francisation et de l’Intégration (MIFI). **Les AEC considérées doivent compter au moins 1000h de formation. Toute autre combinaison d’AEC en bureautique et d’expérience pertinente sera analysée. *** Par souci de confidentialité, il est important de caviarder les informations personnelles apparaissant sur vos documents de candidature, telles que le code permanent, la date de naissance, etc. Veuillez vous assurer de laisser les informations nominatives, ainsi que les informations de réussite scolaire visibles. Conditions de travail et rémunération Les secrétaires d’écoles doivent être disponibles dès 7h30 le matin. Taux horaire variant selon votre scolarité et vos expériences de travail, ainsi que selon le corps d’emploi dans lequel vous pourriez être affecté: À compter du 1er avril 2026 · Agent(e) de bureau classe 2 24,90$/h à 25,95$/h · Agent(e) de bureau classe 1 25,61$/h à 28,65$/h · Secrétaire 25,42$/h à 27,65$/h · Secrétaire d’école 26,15$/h à 31,06$/h *Les attestations d’expérience pertinentes à la fonction doivent être déposées au plus tard 30 jours suivant l’entrée en fonction pour que l’ajustement salarial soit rétroactif. Ces attestations doivent comporter les informations suivantes : fonction exercée, date de début et date de fin, nombre d’heures travaillées, nom de l’employeur, adresse et signature de ce dernier. Les attestations d’expérience seront analysées par le Bureau de la dotation. Pour postuler Cliquez ici pour déposer votre candidature et contribuer à la mission éducative du plus grand Centre de services scolaire au Québec. Date limite pour postuler : 12 avril 2026 Le CSSDM remercie les candidates et candidats de leur intérêt. Toutefois, veuillez noter que l’équipe du recrutement ne communiquera qu’avec les personnes présélectionnées pour la suite du processus, et ce, en fonction des besoins que présente le CSSDM. Le CSSDM s’est doté d’un Programme d’accès à l’égalité en emploi et invite les femmes, les membres des minorités visibles, les membres des minorités ethniques, les Autochtones et les personnes handicapées à présenter leur candidature. Les personnes handicapées qui le désirent peuvent recevoir de l’assistance pour le processus de présélection et de sélection. Le personnel du CSSDM est soumis à laLoi sur la laïcité de l’État(la «LLÉ») ainsi que depuis le 30 octobre 2025 à laLoi visant notamment à renforcer la laïcité dans le réseau de l’éducation et modifiant diverses dispositions législatives(la «LRL»). La LLÉ et la LRL prévoient notamment que le CSSDM respecte la laïcité de l’état et ses principes, incluant la séparation de l’état et des religions, la neutralité religieuse de l’État, l’égalité de tous les citoyens et citoyennes, dont l’égalité entre les femmes et les hommes, ainsi que la liberté de conscience et la liberté de religion. La LRL prévoit, entre autres choses, l’interdiction du port d’un signe religieux à tout membre du personnel du centre de services scolaire qui se trouve sur les lieux mis à la disposition d’une école ou d’un centre ou est en présence d’un élève. L’interdiction s’applique au personnel embauché après le 19 mars 2025 ou ayant changé de fonction après cette date. Ces lois prévoient également l’obligation pour l’ensemble du personnel du CSSDM d’exercer ses fonctions à visage découvert. De plus, la LRL a également pour objet de promouvoir, notamment dans le cadre des services éducatifs, la qualité du français, seule langue commune de la nation québécoise, au sein du système scolaire public afin de permettre l’adhésion et la contribution de tous à la culture distincte de cette nation. Domaine: Administration et gestion, Service clientèle et soutien administratif 35h heures / semaine Jour, Jour, Temps partiel, Temps plein Emploi Temporaire En présentiel

Sanexen is seeking a Mechanical Engineer for its Brossard offices.

Job Description

As part of our growth across Canada, we are looking to strengthen our engineering department to provide structural technical support to project teams and business lines. We are currently seeking a Mechanical Engineer to join the team.

Main responsibilities

  • Technology Selection: Identify and select treatment technologies in collaboration with project teams to meet technical requirements for bids and projects, while considering contractual, commercial, cost, schedule, resource, risk, and quality constraints.
  • Mechanical Design: Perform the design and mechanical sizing of systems, equipment, and installations related to environmental and treatment projects (water, soil, and air).
  • Detailed Engineering Calculations: Execute mechanical calculations required for detailed engineering, including pressure drops, pump selection, piping, mechanical stress, supports, strength of materials, vibration, and fatigue.
  • Documentation & CAD: Participate in the development of mechanical plans, diagrams, piping isometrics, and detailed engineering for “Issued for Construction” (IFC) plans.
  • Equipment Specification: Select, specify, and coordinate mechanical equipment (pumps, piping, tanks, dosing systems, rotating equipment, and associated structures) for internal construction or for specialized subcontractors and suppliers.
  • Engineering Transfer: Plan, structure, and collaborate on the transfer of engineering data to project and operational teams responsible for construction, mobilization, commissioning, and operation of technologies and assets.
  • Technical Support: Participate in mechanical commissioning, technical troubleshooting, and optimization of equipment and systems as required.
  • Testing & Analysis: Plan, supervise, and analyze laboratory or pilot-scale tests; perform data analysis to evaluate system or process efficiency and write technical reports.
  • Technical Reference: Act as an internal technical reference for mechanical engineering within multidisciplinary teams, ensuring technical quality, consistency of engineering solutions, and the development of internal expertise.
  • Expert Collaboration: Serve as a technical expert on specific mandates related to major environmental projects throughout Canada.
  • Continuous Improvement: Participate in the improvement of engineering methods, procedures, standards, and practices, including change management and risk analysis, with an emphasis on mechanical risks.
  • Development: Maintain a high level of competency through continuous training and mentoring while developing distinctive technical expertise.

Qualifications required

Sought Profile

  • 4 to 10 years of relevant experience in mechanical engineering, equipment design, or industrial facility engineering.
  • University degree in Mechanical Engineering or an equivalent field.
  • Solid mastery of design principles and mechanical engineering applied to complex problem-solving with a practical, solution-oriented approach.
  • Member or eligible for membership with the Ordre des ingénieurs du Québec (OIQ) or equivalent in another province.
  • Proficiency in the Microsoft Office Suite and comfort with mechanical design tools (e.g., AutoCAD, Inventor, SolidWorks, or equivalent).
  • Excellent command of French (oral and written).
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively in a team.
  • Valid driver’s license.

Assets

  • Proficiency in English.
  • Possession of the ASP Construction certification (Health and Safety on Construction Sites).

Proficiency in French and English:
Given the diversity of our team and the need to work with local, pan-Canadian, and international clients and partners, the ability to understand and communicate in both languages is required.

We value diversity and inclusion and are committed to providing a respectful and equitable work environment for all.

description: Climate, energy, politics, social issues Hiring: Growth Manager Organization: Canada's National Observer (CNO) Location: Anywhere in Canada (Vancouver or Toronto preferred) The Mission Canada's National Observer is an independent digital news outlet founded in 2015, publishing reporting and analysis on climate, energy, politics, and social issues. We have built a loyal audience of more than 4.5 million annual readers, 45,000 newsletter subscribers, and more than 400,000 institutional subscribers from universities, government bodies, and civil society organizations across Canada and abroad. We made history as the first digital-only publication to win a National Newspaper Award, and our investigations have set the agenda and brought about change in both the public and private sectors. We are a deeply experienced team doing outsized work — and we need the right person to help us grow. CNO is seeking a high-energy, self-motivated Growth Manager to join our senior leadership team. We are looking for a driven operator — someone who thrives on execution, translates strategy into action, and builds scalable systems that grow subscription revenue and audience month over month. The Mandate CNO's Publisher sets the company's strategic direction. Your job is to own the execution of it on the business side — taking a clear mission and making it work in the market. You will lead our subscription growth and crowdfunding efforts with a builder's mindset and a collaborative spirit: Execute & Pivot: You envision and create systems for revenue and marketing; when they work, you scale them. When they don't, you pivot with speed and data-driven insight. You will forge new strategies — and bring the Publisher into decisions that shift direction. Think Creatively: You aren't afraid to challenge conventional approaches to digital media paywalls or audience development, and you bring fresh ideas to the table for leadership to consider. Operational Ownership: You manage the product budget and direct external contractors within approved parameters, and you are the lead executor on the business side of our digital assets. You are CNO's lead on marketing — owning the strategy and execution across all channels, from email campaigns to crowdfunding drives to podcast and program launches to subscription conversion. Revenue Accountability: You will help shape CNO's annual revenue targets in collaboration with the Publisher, then own the execution required to meet them. This is not a support role — it is a performance role, and results matter. Your Responsibilities Daily Immersion You are expected to read, watch, and listen to CNO content every day. This is not optional. You will regularly audit the user journey — identifying friction, spotting opportunities, and bringing recommendations to the Publisher. You cannot write compelling CTAs or build effective funnels without understanding what our journalism means to our audience. Revenue Systems The core measure of success in this role is straightforward: subscription revenue must grow month over month against the prior year. You will build on an established program with proven momentum, inherit systems that work, and your mandate is to accelerate them. Work closely with our Technology Lead and design team to optimize the end-to-end subscriber journey and crowdfunding funnels across all CNO platforms — the website, newsletters, podcasts, and video. Manage advertising placement directly or through contractors of your selection. During fundraising campaigns, manage and direct campaign contractors to maintain momentum and quality. Project Management & Creative Liaison Serve as the bridge between the business side and our design and technology teams — translating revenue goals into briefs, managing timelines, and ensuring high-quality output from internal leads and external contractors. Write value-driven CTAs that speak to CNO's mission and embed them seamlessly in the user experience. Leverage AI tools to accelerate content production, analyze funnel performance, and streamline communication across teams. Strategic Budgeting Participate in CNO's leadership budget meetings alongside the Publisher and senior team, bringing data-driven proposals for resource allocation. Within the approved budget, allocate resources where they will have the highest ROI for audience growth and retention, and bring proposals for significant shifts to the Publisher. Team Alignment Chair the weekly business sprint to review KPIs, identify bottlenecks, and adjust the roadmap in real-time, keeping the Publisher informed of progress and obstacles. Who You Are Genuinely Excited: You are looking for an organization worth working hard for. CNO's journalism — on climate, politics, and the forces shaping Canada's future — genuinely moves you. That enthusiasm isn't a nice-to-have; it's the spark that will ignite our revenue generation machine. What can we make happen? How can we go further together? Those questions drive you. You love a challenge and relish hitting goals. High Energy & Self-Directed You don't wait for instructions on execution. You see a gap in the funnel and you build a bridge to close it — then you report back on what you learned. Strong Writer and Communicator You can speak and write fluently about politics, journalism, and society's challenges. You can learn to connect the dots between CNO's editorial mission and its audience's reasons to subscribe and give. Systems Thinker You love creating workflows that make the company run smoother and more profitably, and you document what you build so it scales. You always keep ROI front of mind and take pride in bringing in new business. Collaborative by Nature: You want to be a significant contributor in a company that values creative thinking — and you understand that great execution requires trust built through communication, not just results. Comfortable in the Middle You translate between the language of business goals and the language of design and technology without losing either side. You hold context across teams and keep projects moving. AI-Fluent You use AI tools to move faster and think bigger — drafting, researching, analyzing, automating the repetitive so you can focus on the strategic. You're not looking for AI to replace your judgment; you're looking for it to extend your reach. You use AI to teach yourself how to use other systems — treating it as your always-available onboarding partner for new tools, platforms, and workflows. Experienced 8+ years in growth, product, communications, or business development. Media background is a plus, but a builder's mindset, genuine respect for journalism's role in society, and a desire to support CNO's mission are the priorities. Comfortable managing people — setting expectations, giving feedback, and holding contractors and staff accountable to deadlines and quality standards. Comfortable working in Mailchimp, DonorBox, Drupal CMS, and Asana — or able to get up to speed quickly on tools like these. Salary and benefits $95,000 per annum (Starting) + Performance-Based Growth Path Benefits A formal compensation review at 12 months is tied to defined revenue benchmarks. We expect this role to grow. Extended health benefits package including $1000 annually for counseling Four weeks vacation + paid time off between Christmas and New Years RRSP plan with $1,500 matching contribution annually from the company Please submit applications through the Bamboo Portal and include a cover letter and a resume. Please mention you saw this at GoodWork.ca. Any incomplete applications will not be considered. Please be advised we can only contact candidates we wish to interview. Deadline for applications is April 17, 2026 We recognize the importance of a diversified workforce, and we encourage women, First Nations, Inuit & Metis candidates, members of visible minorities & persons with disabilities to apply.

Intertek is searching for a Grain Inspector - Union (Part-time) to join our Caleb Brett team in our Levis, QC office. This is a fantastic opportunity to grow a versatile career in Agricultural field inspection !

Under broad supervision, to render to customers commodity inspection services which are timely, safe, legal, ethical, and effective; to perform the necessary volume measurements, temperature measurements, sampling, calculations, documentation, and reporting which ensure that the customer receives an independent, accurate, and complete assessment of quantity and quality of material.

The Grain Inspector is responsible for :

SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES

  • To prepare for and organize grain inspection jobs so that services are rendered, and reports and samples are submitted, in a timely manner.
  • To attend commodity material movements involving loading and unloading of rail cars or trucks.
  • To perform routine equipment calibration, verification, and function checks.
  • To perform, by specified methodology, visual observation, volume measurement, temperature measurement, and sampling of commodity materials contained or conveyed in rail cars or trucks.
  • To communicate and coordinate with loading facilities and Intertek management personnel to promote the smoother exercise of duties assigned.
  • To verify and communicate the results obtained, and to make the entries into the appropriate media, whether print or electronic, required to ensure the validity and traceability of the information.
  • To maintain work areas, records, and equipment in a clean, organized, and functional condition.
  • To monitor the availability of the supplies needed for the above processes, and to make any needs for such supplies known to the Inspection and Training Coordinator.
  • To assist in the inspection, quality system application and organizational training of less experienced employees by utilizing approved online and printed materials and/or materials supplied by Intertek management.
  • To carry out the above responsibilities, and all others which may be assigned, in a manner demonstrating support for and adherence to the Company’s Safety Policy and Procedures, Quality Policy and Procedures, Ethics Policy, Environmental Management System, Vision and Strategy, and exercise good judgment, common sense, and diplomacy in so doing.

SUPERVISION EXERCISED

  • The position communicates directly with the Manager-Inspection Operations in the day-to-day operations and in communication of work assignments and direction.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • The Grain Inspector must have a grasp of basic mathematics and computer skills, and must, in the opinion of the hiring authority hold a Canadian grain grading certification, minimum level 3.
  • The Grain Inspector must be physically able to do the work required and cannot be afraid of heights or of confined spaces.
  • The Grain Inspector should have a positive attitude, a high tolerance for job pressure and the ability to work and communicate with people of diverse personalities and backgrounds.
  • Language requirements, proficiency in spoken and written English and at least an intermediate level of spoken French, due to daily contact with clients, suppliers, partners, and colleagues outside Quebec.
